# Project

## Bimodule: (S,R)-bimodules and commuting left and right scalar actions

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $S$ and $R$ be unital rings. An **$(S,R)$-bimodule** is an abelian group $N$ that is a left $S$-module and a right $R$-module ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]) such that the two actions commute:

$$(sn)r=s(nr)$$

for every $s\in S$, $n\in N$, and $r\in R$. It is denoted ${}_SN_R$ when the rings need to be displayed.

Every ring $R$ is an $(R,R)$-bimodule by left and right multiplication. If $R$ is commutative, every left $R$-module becomes an $(R,R)$-bimodule by defining $mr:=rm$.

[Alphabeta Math, (S,R)-bimodules and commuting left and right scalar actions, Definition (def-bimodule)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-bimodule)

### Lean statement

Translation source: portal. Alphabeta Math, (S,R)-bimodules and commuting left and right scalar actions (def-bimodule), https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-bimodule. The plan supplies this portal definition as the sole endpoint. The notation ${}_S N_R$ corresponds to Bimodule.1 S R N, with the right action encoded as a left Module over MulOpposite R. The other projections supply the regular-ring and commutative-ring constructions and their action formulas. The defect report at https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects returned HTTP 404, so its contents could not be reviewed. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
def Bimodule : Prod
  (∀ (S : Type u) (R : Type v) (N : Type w) [Ring S] [Ring R] [AddCommGroup N],
    Type (max u v w))
  (Prod
    (∀ (R : Type v) [Ring R],
      Subtype (fun B : Sigma (fun left : Module R R =>
        Subtype (fun right : Module (MulOpposite R) R =>
          letI : SMul R R := left.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
          letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) R := right.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
          SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) R R)) =>
        letI : SMul R R := B.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
        letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) R := B.2.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
        (∀ s n : R, s • n = s * n) ∧
        (∀ n r : R, MulOpposite.op r • n = n * r)))
    (∀ (R : Type v) (N : Type w) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup N] [left : Module R N],
      Subtype (fun B : Sigma (fun l : Module R N =>
        Subtype (fun right : Module (MulOpposite R) N =>
          letI : SMul R N := l.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
          letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) N := right.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
          SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) R N)) =>
        B.1 = left ∧
        (letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) N := B.2.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
         ∀ (r : R) (n : N), MulOpposite.op r • n = r • n)))) := ⟨(fun S R N _ _ _ =>
    Sigma (fun left : Module S N =>
      Subtype (fun right : Module (MulOpposite R) N =>
        letI : SMul S N := left.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
        letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) N := right.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
        SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) S N))),
  ⟨(fun R _ =>
      let left : Module R R := Semiring.toModule
      let right : Module (MulOpposite R) R := Semiring.toOppositeModule
      letI : SMul R R := left.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
      letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) R := right.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
      ⟨⟨left, ⟨right,
          show SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) R R from Semigroup.opposite_smulCommClass⟩⟩,
        ⟨(fun _ _ => rfl), (fun _ _ => rfl)⟩⟩),
    (fun R N _ _ left =>
      letI : Module R N := left
      let right : Module (MulOpposite R) N :=
        Module.compHom N (RingHom.fromOpposite (RingHom.id R) (fun a b => mul_comm a b))
      letI : SMul R N := left.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
      letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) N := right.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
      ⟨⟨left, ⟨right, show SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) R N from
          ⟨fun r s n => show MulOpposite.unop r • (s • n) = s • (MulOpposite.unop r • n) from
            by
              simpa only [← mul_smul] using
                congrArg (fun a : R => a • n) (mul_comm (MulOpposite.unop r) s)⟩⟩⟩,
        ⟨rfl, (fun _ _ => rfl)⟩⟩)⟩⟩
```

## RegularModuleRightAction: F(A) is a (B,A)-bimodule for every additive functor F

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $A$ and $B$ be unital rings and let
$F:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ be an additive functor
([[def-additive-functor]]). On the left $B$-module $M=F(A)$ define, for
$a\in A$ and $m\in M$,

$$ma:=F(r_a)(m),$$

where $r_a:A\to A$, $r_a(x)=xa$, is right multiplication, a left $A$-linear
endomorphism of $A$. Together with the given left $B$-action this makes $M$ a
$(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]): the right $A$-action satisfies the unit,
associativity and distributivity laws of [[def-left-and-right-modules]] and
commutes with the left $B$-action. No commutativity of the rings is assumed and
no choice is used.

[Alphabeta Math, F(A) is a (B,A)-bimodule for every additive functor F, Statement (lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action)

### Lean statement

Translation source: portal. The plan designates the statement from Alphabeta Math, F(A) is a (B,A)-bimodule for every additive functor F (lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action), as the endpoint. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action

ULift represents the regular left A-module in the source carrier universe and transports right multiplication to that representative. The Lean check constructed the specified bimodule without choice. The defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, so its contents could not be reviewed. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem RegularModuleRightAction : ∀ (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [Ring A] [Ring B]
  (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u z} A) (ModuleCat.{w} B))
  [CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F],
  let regular := ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{z} A)
  let lift := LinearEquiv.symm (ULift.moduleEquiv : ULift.{z} A ≃ₗ[A] A)
  let M := CategoryTheory.Functor.obj F regular
  ∃ N : Bimodule.1 B A M,
    N.1 = ModuleCat.isModule M ∧
    ∀ (a : A) (m : M),
      @SMul.smul (MulOpposite A) M
        N.2.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul (MulOpposite.op a) m =
      ModuleCat.Hom.hom
        (CategoryTheory.Functor.map F
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearEquiv.conjRingEquiv lift (LinearMap.mulRight A a)))) m
```

## CanonicalWattsComparison: The canonical comparison to the tensor functor of F(A) is balanced and natural

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $A,B$ be unital rings, let
$F:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ be additive, and let $M=F(A)$
carry the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure of
[[lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action]]. For
$x\in X$ let $\ell_x:A\to X$, $\ell_x(a)=ax$. Then

$$\beta_X:M\times X\to F(X),\qquad \beta_X(m,x)=F(\ell_x)(m),$$

is balanced ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]]) and $B$-linear in $m$, so it
induces a unique group homomorphism

$$\tau_X:M\otimes_AX\to F(X),\qquad \tau_X(m\otimes x)=F(\ell_x)(m),$$

and each $\tau_X$ is $B$-linear. Moreover
$\tau:M\otimes_A-\Rightarrow F$ is natural:
$F(u)\circ\tau_X=\tau_Y\circ(1_M\otimes u)$ for every left $A$-linear
$u:X\to Y$ ([[def-natural-transformation]]). The construction of $\tau$ chooses
no presentation of $X$ and no elements.

[Alphabeta Math, The canonical comparison to the tensor functor of F(A) is balanced and natural, Statement (lem-canonical-eilenberg-watts-comparison-is-balanced-and-natural)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-canonical-eilenberg-watts-comparison-is-balanced-and-natural)

### Lean statement

Translation source: portal. The plan supplies this portal statement as the endpoint and gives no article statement. Alphabeta Math, The canonical comparison to the tensor functor of F(A) is balanced and natural, Statement (lem-canonical-eilenberg-watts-comparison-is-balanced-and-natural). https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-canonical-eilenberg-watts-comparison-is-balanced-and-natural

The right action uses the formula of RegularModuleRightAction. The tensor uses the additive quotient on pairs by biadditivity and balance. The scalar action and functor map are specified on elementary tensors. The natural transformation uses the canonical universe lift of F, and transporting its components back to F(X) gives the unique additive extension of beta as a B-linear map. The characterization uses the elements of X as variables and requires no presentation or chosen elements of X.

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, so the report could not be reviewed. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem CanonicalWattsComparison : ∀ (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [Ring A] [Ring B]
  (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u z} A) (ModuleCat.{w} B))
  [CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F],
  let regular := ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{z} A)
  let down : LinearEquiv (RingHom.id A) (ULift.{z} A) A := ULift.moduleEquiv
  let FX : ModuleCat.{max u z} A → ModuleCat.{w} B := CategoryTheory.Functor.obj F
  let M := FX regular
  let right : A → M → M := fun a m =>
    ModuleCat.Hom.hom (CategoryTheory.Functor.map F
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearEquiv.conjRingEquiv (LinearEquiv.symm down)
        (LinearMap.mulRight A a)))) m
  let ell : ∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A), X → ModuleCat.Hom regular X :=
    fun _X x => ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearEquiv.toLinearMap down) x)
  let beta : ∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A), M → X → ModuleCat.carrier (FX X) :=
    fun X m x => ModuleCat.Hom.hom (CategoryTheory.Functor.map F (ell X x)) m
  let Free := fun (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A) => Finsupp (Prod M X) Int
  let gen : ∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A), M → X → Free X :=
    fun _X m x => Finsupp.single (m, x) 1
  let relations : ∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A), AddSubgroup (Free X) := fun X =>
    AddSubgroup.closure
      { p | (∃ (m m' : M) (x : X), p = gen X (m + m') x - gen X m x - gen X m' x) ∨
        (∃ (m : M) (x x' : X), p = gen X m (x + x') - gen X m x - gen X m x') ∨
        (∃ (a : A) (m : M) (x : X), p = gen X (right a m) x - gen X m (a • x)) }
  let Tensor := fun X => HasQuotient.Quotient (Free X) (relations X)
  let pure : ∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A), M → X → Tensor X :=
    fun X m x => QuotientAddGroup.mk' (relations X) (gen X m x)
  (∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A),
    (∀ (m m' : M) (x : X), beta X (m + m') x = beta X m x + beta X m' x) ∧
    (∀ (m : M) (x x' : X), beta X m (x + x') = beta X m x + beta X m x') ∧
    (∀ (a : A) (m : M) (x : X), beta X (right a m) x = beta X m (a • x)) ∧
    (∀ (b : B) (m : M) (x : X), beta X (b • m) x = b • beta X m x)) ∧
  (∃ (tensorModule : ∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A), Module B (Tensor X)),
    let obj : ModuleCat.{max u z} A → ModuleCat.{max u z w} B := fun X =>
      @ModuleCat.of B _ (Tensor X) (QuotientAddGroup.Quotient.addCommGroup (relations X))
        (tensorModule X)
    ∃ (map : ∀ {X Y : ModuleCat.{max u z} A}, ModuleCat.Hom X Y → ModuleCat.Hom (obj X) (obj Y))
      (mapId : ∀ X, @map X X (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id X) =
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (obj X))
      (mapComp : ∀ {X Y Z : ModuleCat.{max u z} A} (f : ModuleCat.Hom X Y) (g : ModuleCat.Hom Y Z),
        @map X Z (@CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp _ _ X Y Z f g) =
          @CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp _ _ (obj X) (obj Y) (obj Z)
            (@map X Y f) (@map Y Z g)),
      let T : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u z} A) (ModuleCat.{max u z w} B) :=
        CategoryTheory.Functor.mk obj (@map) mapId (@mapComp)
      let liftedF := CategoryTheory.Functor.comp F (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{max u z, w} B)
      ∃ tau : CategoryTheory.NatTrans T liftedF,
        (∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A) (b : B) (m : M) (x : X),
          letI : Module B (Tensor X) := tensorModule X
          b • pure X m x = pure X (b • m) x) ∧
        (∀ (X Y : ModuleCat.{max u z} A) (f : ModuleCat.Hom X Y) (m : M) (x : X),
          ModuleCat.Hom.hom (CategoryTheory.Functor.map T f) (pure X m x) =
            pure Y m (ModuleCat.Hom.hom f x)) ∧
        (∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u z} A),
          letI : Module B (Tensor X) := tensorModule X
          let tauX : LinearMap (RingHom.id B) (Tensor X) (FX X) := LinearMap.comp
            (LinearEquiv.toLinearMap (ULift.moduleEquiv :
              LinearEquiv (RingHom.id B) (ULift.{max u z} (FX X)) (FX X)))
            (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app tau X))
          (∀ (m : M) (x : X), tauX (pure X m x) = beta X m x) ∧
          (∀ h : AddMonoidHom (Tensor X) (FX X),
            (∀ (m : M) (x : X), h (pure X m x) = beta X m x) →
              h = LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom tauX)))
```

## NaturalTransformationsOfTensorFunctors: Natural transformations between tensor functors are bimodule maps

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $A,B$ be unital rings and let $M,M'$ be $(B,A)$-bimodules
([[def-bimodule]]), with tensor functors $T_M=M\otimes_A-$ and
$T_{M'}=M'\otimes_A-$. Under the tensor-unit isomorphisms
$\rho_M:M\otimes_AA\to M$ and $\rho_{M'}:M'\otimes_AA\to M'$ of
[[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]], every natural
transformation $\eta:T_M\Rightarrow T_{M'}$ corresponds to the $B$-linear map

$$f=\rho_{M'}\circ\eta_A\circ\rho_M^{-1}:M\longrightarrow M',\qquad f(m)=\rho_{M'}\bigl(\eta_A(m\otimes1)\bigr),$$

which satisfies $f(ma)=f(m)a$ for all $a\in A$, i.e. is a $(B,A)$-bimodule
map, and then $\eta_X=f\otimes1_X$ for every left $A$-module $X$. Conversely
every bimodule map $f:M\to M'$ yields a natural transformation with components
$f\otimes1_X$. The two assignments are inverse bijections
$\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$,
compatible with addition, identities, and vertical composition. No commutativity
and no choice are used. Here $\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})$ uses
bimodule maps as set codes for the component families, not those
proper-class families as elements of a set.

[Alphabeta Math, Natural transformations between tensor functors are bimodule maps, Statement (thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps)

### Lean statement

Translation source: portal. Alphabeta Math, Natural transformations between tensor functors are bimodule maps, Statement (thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps), is the selected endpoint in item.portal. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps

The tensor universal property is pointwise existence and uniqueness. A natural transformation is expressed by the graph of its components, with a unique B-linear map at each object and the usual naturality equations. The bimodule maps are the set codes for these graphs. The shared-slot check in EndpointAudit.lean verified the full proposition and the graph of an ordinary Lean natural transformation. Both axiom audits report propext and Quot.sound, with no Classical.choice.

The 27 November owner clarification in input.request, recorded in owner-clarification.json and in the owner recheck evidence translation-rechecks-f13b4bd8ba9fe139.json, requires termwise eligibility in finite C-linear dot labels. This endpoint quantifies over all (B,A)-bimodule maps.

Ian Xiao’s related Theorem 1.1 appears on printed page 2 of the archived source/mackey-bimodules.pdf (SHA-256 bc57d13777e7df145b6dfd84029e0e9539fedb33d22b2823e14c096e4c3c12f2). The separately retrieved 27 November revision also places Theorem 1.1 on printed page 2 (SHA-256 6d7e885955f23ae6d10d8e8394d3fe9252dfc2fa7ce7ec149ec190de766c978e). Both article passages provide context. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 on recheck, so its contents could not be assessed. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem NaturalTransformationsOfTensorFunctors : ∀ (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [Ring A] [Ring B],
  let Bimod := Sigma (fun M : ModuleCat.{w} B =>
    { D : Bimodule.1 B A M // D.1 = (inferInstance : Module B M) })
  let right := fun (M : Bimod) (m : M.1) (a : A) =>
    letI : Module (MulOpposite A) M.1 := M.2.1.2.1
    MulOpposite.op a • m
  let AMod := ModuleCat.{max u x} A
  let BMod := ModuleCat.{max u w x} B
  let regular := ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{x} A)
  let Balanced := fun (M : Bimod) (X : AMod) (Y : BMod)
      (p : ↥M.1 → X → Y) =>
    (∀ m n : ↥M.1, ∀ a : X, p (m + n) a = p m a + p n a) ∧
    (∀ m : ↥M.1, ∀ a b : X, p m (a + b) = p m a + p m b) ∧
    (∀ b : B, ∀ m : ↥M.1, ∀ a : X, p (b • m) a = b • p m a) ∧
    (∀ a : A, ∀ m : ↥M.1, ∀ y : X, p (right M m a) y = p m (a • y))
  let TensorFunctor := fun (M : Bimod) =>
    { D : Sigma (fun F : CategoryTheory.Functor (AMod) (BMod) =>
        ∀ X : AMod, ↥M.1 → X → F.obj X) //
      (∀ X : AMod, Balanced M X (D.1.obj X) (D.2 X)) ∧
      (∀ (X : AMod) (Y : BMod) (p : ↥M.1 → X → Y),
        Balanced M X Y p →
        ∃! k : LinearMap (RingHom.id B) (D.1.obj X) Y,
          ∀ (m : ↥M.1) (y : X), k (D.2 X m y) = p m y) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : AMod) (h : ModuleCat.Hom X Y) (m : ↥M.1) (y : X),
        (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (D.1.map h)) (D.2 X m y) = D.2 Y m ((ModuleCat.Hom.hom h) y)) }
  let NatCode := fun (M N : Bimod) =>
    {f : LinearMap (RingHom.id B) M.1 N.1 //
      ∀ (m : ↥M.1) (a : A), f (right M m a) = right N (f m) a}
  let Component := fun {M N : Bimod}
      (T : TensorFunctor M) (S : TensorFunctor N) (X : AMod) =>
    LinearMap (RingHom.id B) (T.1.1.obj X) (S.1.1.obj X)
  let NatGraph := fun {M N : Bimod}
      (T : TensorFunctor M) (S : TensorFunctor N) =>
    { G : ∀ X : AMod, Component T S X → Prop //
      (∀ X : AMod, ∃! k : Component T S X, G X k) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : AMod) (h : ModuleCat.Hom X Y)
          (k : Component T S X) (l : Component T S Y),
        G X k → G Y l →
        LinearMap.comp (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (S.1.1.map h)) k =
          LinearMap.comp l (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (T.1.1.map h))) }
  let Unitor := fun {M : Bimod} (T : TensorFunctor M) =>
    LinearEquiv (RingHom.id B) (T.1.1.obj (regular)) M.1
  let IsUnitor := fun {M : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      (rho : Unitor T) =>
    (∀ (m : ↥M.1) (a : A), rho (T.1.2 (regular) m (ULift.up a)) = right M m a) ∧
    (∀ m : ↥M.1, rho.symm m = T.1.2 (regular) m (ULift.up (1 : A)))
  let eval := fun {M N : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      {S : TensorFunctor N} (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S)
      (k : Component T S (regular)) =>
    LinearMap.comp sigma.toLinearMap (LinearMap.comp k rho.symm.toLinearMap)
  let Pure := fun {M N : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      {S : TensorFunctor N} (f : NatCode M N) (X : AMod)
      (k : Component T S X) =>
    ∀ (m : ↥M.1) (y : X), k (T.1.2 X m y) = S.1.2 X (f.1 m) y
  let Represents := fun {M N : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) (eta : NatGraph T S) (f : NatCode M N) =>
    (∀ k : Component T S (regular), eta.1 (regular) k →
      f.1 = eval rho sigma k ∧
      ∀ m : ↥M.1, f.1 m = sigma (k (T.1.2 (regular) m (ULift.up (1 : A))))) ∧
    (∀ (X : AMod) (k : Component T S X), eta.1 X k → Pure f X k)
  let InverseAssignments := fun {M N : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) =>
    (∀ eta : NatGraph T S, ∃! f : NatCode M N, Represents rho sigma eta f) ∧
    (∀ f : NatCode M N, ∃! eta : NatGraph T S, Represents rho sigma eta f)
  let Addition := fun {M N : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) =>
    ∀ eta theta : NatGraph T S,
      ∃ sum : NatGraph T S,
        (∀ (X : AMod) (k l : Component T S X),
          eta.1 X k → theta.1 X l → sum.1 X (k + l)) ∧
        (∀ (k l : Component T S (regular)),
          eta.1 (regular) k → theta.1 (regular) l →
          eval rho sigma (k + l) = eval rho sigma k + eval rho sigma l)
  let Identity := fun {M : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      (rho : Unitor T) =>
    ∃ identity : NatGraph T T,
      (∀ X : AMod, identity.1 X LinearMap.id) ∧
      eval rho rho LinearMap.id = LinearMap.id
  let Composition := fun {M N P : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      {U : TensorFunctor P}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) (tau : Unitor U) =>
    ∀ (eta : NatGraph T S) (theta : NatGraph S U),
      ∃ composite : NatGraph T U,
        (∀ (X : AMod) (k : Component T S X) (l : Component S U X),
          eta.1 X k → theta.1 X l → composite.1 X (LinearMap.comp l k)) ∧
        (∀ (k : Component T S (regular)) (l : Component S U (regular)),
          eta.1 (regular) k → theta.1 (regular) l →
          eval rho tau (LinearMap.comp l k) =
            LinearMap.comp (eval sigma tau l) (eval rho sigma k))
  ∀ (M N P : Bimod) (T : TensorFunctor M) (S : TensorFunctor N) (U : TensorFunctor P),
    ∃ (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) (tau : Unitor U),
      IsUnitor rho ∧ IsUnitor sigma ∧ IsUnitor tau ∧
      InverseAssignments rho sigma ∧ InverseAssignments sigma tau ∧ InverseAssignments rho tau ∧
      Addition rho sigma ∧ Identity rho ∧ Composition rho sigma tau
```

## SmallProjectiveGenerator: Small projective generators and progenerators

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small cocomplete abelian category. An object $P$ of $\mathcal C$ is a **small projective generator** when (i) $P$ is projective ([[def-projective-object]]), (ii) $P$ is a generator ([[def-generator-and-cogenerator-of-a-category]]), and (iii) the abelian-group-valued functor $\mathcal C(P,-):\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Ab}$ preserves every set-indexed coproduct ([[def-preservation-reflection-creation-continuity-and-cocontinuity]], [[def-products-and-coproducts]]). Here "small" names this compactness property of the functor $\mathcal C(P,-)$; it does not assert that the underlying object, set, or module is small. For a unital ring $B$, a left $B$-module $P$ is a **progenerator** when $P$ is finitely generated ([[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]]), projective ([[def-projective-module]]), and a generator. For module categories the two notions agree: a left $B$-module is a small projective generator of $B\text{-Mod}$ if and only if it is a progenerator ([[lem-small-projective-modules-are-exactly-finitely-generated-projective-modules]]), and in particular the regular module ${}_BB$ is a small projective generator. No commutativity of $B$ is assumed, and both phrases are properties of an object, not existence axioms beyond the coproducts already required of $\mathcal C$.

[Alphabeta Math, Small projective generators and progenerators, Definition (def-small-projective-generator-and-progenerator)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-small-projective-generator-and-progenerator)

```lean
  (Σ smallInModules : ∀ (B : Type v) [Ring B], ModuleCat.{v} B → Prop,
    { progenerator : ∀ (B : Type v) [Ring B], ModuleCat.{v} B → Prop //
      (∀ (B : Type v) [Ring B] (P : ModuleCat.{v} B),
        smallInModules B P ↔ progenerator B P) ∧
```

## ModuleTensorUniversalProperty: Universal property of M⊗_RN

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $R$ be a unital ring, $M$ a right $R$-module, $N$ a left $R$-module, and

$$\tau:M\times N\longrightarrow M\otimes_RN,\qquad \tau(m,n)=m\otimes n.$$

The map $\tau$ is balanced ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]]). For every abelian group $A$ and every balanced map $b:M\times N\to A$, there is a unique group homomorphism

$$\overline b:M\otimes_RN\longrightarrow A$$

such that $\overline b(m\otimes n)=b(m,n)$ for all $m,n$. Consequently composition with $\tau$ is a bijection

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ab}}(M\otimes_RN,A)\cong\operatorname{Bal}_R(M,N;A).$$

[Alphabeta Math, Universal property of M⊗_RN, Statement (thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products)

### Lean statement

Translation source: portal. Alphabeta Math, Universal property of M⊗_RN, Statement (thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products), https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products. The plan selects this portal statement as the endpoint and supplies no article statement. The tensor product uses the quotient of the free abelian group of finitely supported integer coefficients on pairs by the two additivity relations and the scalar balance relation. The elementary tensor is the image of its basis generator. The right R-action is written as a left action of MulOpposite R. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, so the report could not be read. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ModuleTensorUniversalProperty : ∀ (R : Type u) (M : Type v) (N : Type w) [Ring R]
  [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module (MulOpposite R) M] [Module R N],
  let F := Finsupp (Prod M N) Int
  let gen : Prod M N → F := fun p => Finsupp.single p 1
  let H : AddSubgroup F := AddSubgroup.closure
    { x | (∃ (m m' : M) (n : N),
        x = gen (m + m', n) - gen (m, n) - gen (m', n)) ∨
      (∃ (m : M) (n n' : N),
        x = gen (m, n + n') - gen (m, n) - gen (m, n')) ∨
      (∃ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N),
        x = gen (MulOpposite.op r • m, n) - gen (m, r • n)) }
  let T := HasQuotient.Quotient F H
  let τ : Prod M N → T := fun p => QuotientAddGroup.mk' H (gen p)
  ((∀ (m m' : M) (n : N), τ (m + m', n) = τ (m, n) + τ (m', n)) ∧
    (∀ (m : M) (n n' : N), τ (m, n + n') = τ (m, n) + τ (m, n')) ∧
    (∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), τ (MulOpposite.op r • m, n) = τ (m, r • n))) ∧
  (∀ (A : Type z) [AddCommGroup A],
    let Bal := { b : Prod M N → A //
      (∀ (m m' : M) (n : N), b (m + m', n) = b (m, n) + b (m', n)) ∧
      (∀ (m : M) (n n' : N), b (m, n + n') = b (m, n) + b (m, n')) ∧
      (∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), b (MulOpposite.op r • m, n) = b (m, r • n)) }
    (∀ b : Bal, ∃! lift : AddMonoidHom T A, ∀ m n, lift (τ (m, n)) = b.val (m, n)) ∧
    (∃ e : Equiv (AddMonoidHom T A) Bal, ∀ f p, (e f).val p = f (τ p)))
```

## BalancedTensorAssociativity: Associativity of tensor products for compatible bimodules

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

Let $M$ be a right $R$-module, let ${}_RN_S$ be an $(R,S)$-bimodule, and let $P$ be a left $S$-module. There is a canonical group isomorphism

$$\alpha_{M,N,P}:(M\otimes_RN)\otimes_SP\longrightarrow M\otimes_R(N\otimes_SP)$$

determined by

$$\alpha_{M,N,P}((m\otimes n)\otimes p)=m\otimes(n\otimes p).$$

It respects any compatible outer module actions and is natural in $M,N,P$.

[Alphabeta Math, Associativity of tensor products for compatible bimodules, Statement (thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products)

### Lean statement

Translation source: portal. The plan selects Alphabeta Math, Associativity of tensor products for compatible bimodules, Statement (thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products) as the endpoint. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products Each tensor quotient uses the additivity and scalar balance relations of ModuleTensorUniversalProperty. Right module actions are represented by left modules over the opposite rings. The inner and outer induced actions are specified by their elementary-tensor formulas, and the naturality square uses linear maps in the outer variables and bimodule maps in the middle variable. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with a work-in-progress page, so the report could not be read. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem BalancedTensorAssociativity : ∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [Ring R] [Ring S],
  let Middle := Sigma (fun N : ModuleCat.{x} R =>
    { right : Module (MulOpposite S) N //
      letI := right
      SMulCommClass (MulOpposite S) R N })
  let Triple := Prod (ModuleCat.{w} (MulOpposite R)) (Prod Middle (ModuleCat.{y} S))
  let first := fun (X : Triple) => X.1
  let middle := fun (X : Triple) => X.2.1.1
  let last := fun (X : Triple) => X.2.2
  let rightMiddle := fun (X : Triple) => X.2.1.2.val
  let innerLeft := fun (X : Triple) =>
    let M := first X
    let N := middle X
    let F := Finsupp (Prod M N) Int
    let gen : M → N → F := fun a b => Finsupp.single (a, b) 1
    let H : AddSubgroup F := AddSubgroup.closure
      { z | (∃ (a a' : M) (b : N),
              z = gen (a + a') b - gen a b - gen a' b) ∨
            (∃ (a : M) (b b' : N),
              z = gen a (b + b') - gen a b - gen a b') ∨
            (∃ (r : R) (a : M) (b : N),
              z = gen (MulOpposite.op r • a) b - gen a (r • b)) }
    (⟨H, fun m n => QuotientAddGroup.mk' H (gen m n)⟩ :
      Sigma (fun K : AddSubgroup F => M → N → HasQuotient.Quotient F K))
  let innerRight := fun (X : Triple) =>
    let N := middle X
    let P := last X
    letI := rightMiddle X
    let F := Finsupp (Prod N P) Int
    let gen : N → P → F := fun a b => Finsupp.single (a, b) 1
    let H : AddSubgroup F := AddSubgroup.closure
      { z | (∃ (a a' : N) (b : P),
              z = gen (a + a') b - gen a b - gen a' b) ∨
            (∃ (a : N) (b b' : P),
              z = gen a (b + b') - gen a b - gen a b') ∨
            (∃ (r : S) (a : N) (b : P),
              z = gen (MulOpposite.op r • a) b - gen a (r • b)) }
    (⟨H, fun n p => QuotientAddGroup.mk' H (gen n p)⟩ :
      Sigma (fun K : AddSubgroup F => N → P → HasQuotient.Quotient F K))
  let MN := fun (X : Triple) =>
    HasQuotient.Quotient (Finsupp (Prod (first X) (middle X)) Int) (innerLeft X).1
  let NP := fun (X : Triple) =>
    HasQuotient.Quotient (Finsupp (Prod (middle X) (last X)) Int) (innerRight X).1
  let InnerActions := fun (X : Triple) =>
    { a : Prod (Module (MulOpposite S) (MN X)) (Module R (NP X)) //
      (∀ (s : S) (m : first X) (n : middle X),
        a.1.smul (MulOpposite.op s) ((innerLeft X).2 m n) =
          (innerLeft X).2 m ((rightMiddle X).smul (MulOpposite.op s) n)) ∧
      (∀ (r : R) (n : middle X) (p : last X),
        a.2.smul r ((innerRight X).2 n p) = (innerRight X).2 (r • n) p) }
  let Parenthesized := Sigma InnerActions
  let left := fun (X : Parenthesized) =>
    let M := first X.1
    let N := middle X.1
    let P := last X.1
    let A := MN X.1
    letI := X.2.val.1
    let F := Finsupp (Prod A P) Int
    let gen : A → P → F := fun a b => Finsupp.single (a, b) 1
    let H : AddSubgroup F := AddSubgroup.closure
      { z | (∃ (a a' : A) (b : P),
              z = gen (a + a') b - gen a b - gen a' b) ∨
            (∃ (a : A) (b b' : P),
              z = gen a (b + b') - gen a b - gen a b') ∨
            (∃ (r : S) (a : A) (b : P),
              z = gen (MulOpposite.op r • a) b - gen a (r • b)) }
    (⟨H, fun m n p => QuotientAddGroup.mk' H (gen ((innerLeft X.1).2 m n) p)⟩ :
      Sigma (fun K : AddSubgroup F => M → N → P → HasQuotient.Quotient F K))
  let right := fun (X : Parenthesized) =>
    let M := first X.1
    let N := middle X.1
    let P := last X.1
    let B := NP X.1
    letI := X.2.val.2
    let F := Finsupp (Prod M B) Int
    let gen : M → B → F := fun a b => Finsupp.single (a, b) 1
    let H : AddSubgroup F := AddSubgroup.closure
      { z | (∃ (a a' : M) (b : B),
              z = gen (a + a') b - gen a b - gen a' b) ∨
            (∃ (a : M) (b b' : B),
              z = gen a (b + b') - gen a b - gen a b') ∨
            (∃ (r : R) (a : M) (b : B),
              z = gen (MulOpposite.op r • a) b - gen a (r • b)) }
    (⟨H, fun m n p => QuotientAddGroup.mk' H (gen m ((innerRight X.1).2 n p))⟩ :
      Sigma (fun K : AddSubgroup F => M → N → P → HasQuotient.Quotient F K))
  let L := fun (X : Parenthesized) =>
    HasQuotient.Quotient (Finsupp (Prod (MN X.1) (last X.1)) Int) (left X).1
  let T := fun (X : Parenthesized) =>
    HasQuotient.Quotient (Finsupp (Prod (first X.1) (NP X.1)) Int) (right X).1
  let tL := fun (X : Parenthesized) => (left X).2
  let tT := fun (X : Parenthesized) => (right X).2
  (∀ X : Triple, Nonempty (InnerActions X)) ∧
  (∃ α : ∀ X : Parenthesized, AddEquiv (L X) (T X),
    (∀ (X : Parenthesized) (e : AddEquiv (L X) (T X)),
      (∀ (m : first X.1) (n : middle X.1) (p : last X.1),
        e (tL X m n p) = tT X m n p) ↔ e = α X) ∧
    (∀ (X : Parenthesized) (C : Type z) [Ring C] [Module C (first X.1)]
        [SMulCommClass C (MulOpposite R) (first X.1)],
      ∃ (aL : Module C (L X)) (aT : Module C (T X)),
        (∀ (c : C) (m : first X.1) (n : middle X.1) (p : last X.1),
          aL.smul c (tL X m n p) = tL X (c • m) n p ∧
          aT.smul c (tT X m n p) = tT X (c • m) n p) ∧
        (∀ (c : C) (q : L X), α X (aL.smul c q) = aT.smul c (α X q))) ∧
    (∀ (X : Parenthesized) (D : Type t) [Ring D] [Module (MulOpposite D) (last X.1)]
        [SMulCommClass S (MulOpposite D) (last X.1)],
      ∃ (aL : Module (MulOpposite D) (L X)) (aT : Module (MulOpposite D) (T X)),
        (∀ (d : D) (m : first X.1) (n : middle X.1) (p : last X.1),
          aL.smul (MulOpposite.op d) (tL X m n p) = tL X m n (MulOpposite.op d • p) ∧
          aT.smul (MulOpposite.op d) (tT X m n p) = tT X m n (MulOpposite.op d • p)) ∧
        (∀ (d : D) (q : L X),
          α X (aL.smul (MulOpposite.op d) q) = aT.smul (MulOpposite.op d) (α X q))) ∧
    (∀ (X Y : Parenthesized)
        (f : LinearMap (RingHom.id (MulOpposite R)) (first X.1) (first Y.1))
        (g : LinearMap (RingHom.id R) (middle X.1) (middle Y.1))
        (h : LinearMap (RingHom.id S) (last X.1) (last Y.1)),
      (∀ (s : S) (n : middle X.1),
        g ((rightMiddle X.1).smul (MulOpposite.op s) n) =
          (rightMiddle Y.1).smul (MulOpposite.op s) (g n)) →
      let TensorMaps := Prod (AddMonoidHom (L X) (L Y)) (AddMonoidHom (T X) (T Y))
      let induced := fun (maps : TensorMaps) =>
        ∀ (m : first X.1) (n : middle X.1) (p : last X.1),
          maps.1 (tL X m n p) = tL Y (f m) (g n) (h p) ∧
          maps.2 (tT X m n p) = tT Y (f m) (g n) (h p)
      (∃ maps : TensorMaps, induced maps) ∧
      (∀ maps : TensorMaps, induced maps → ∀ q : L X, α Y (maps.1 q) = maps.2 (α X q))))
```

## BimoduleTensorBicategoryCoherence: The Morita data satisfy the bicategory coherence axioms

Prerequisite; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

No original article statement.

### Alphabeta Math

The data of [[def-morita-bicategory-of-rings-and-bimodules]] satisfy the bicategory axioms of [[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]]. Explicitly: for a $(D,C)$-bimodule $H$, a $(C,B)$-bimodule $G$, and a $(B,A)$-bimodule $F$ the canonical associativity isomorphisms are natural isomorphisms of bimodules
$$\alpha_{H,G,F}:(H\otimes_CG)\otimes_BF\longrightarrow H\otimes_C(G\otimes_BF);$$
the unitors $B\otimes_BF\cong F$ and $F\otimes_AA\cong F$ are natural isomorphisms; the pentagon and triangle identities hold; and horizontal composition of bimodule maps, $(g,f)\mapsto g\otimes f$, is a functor on hom-categories that preserves identities and composition. Consequently the composition functors, associator, and unitors make the Morita data a genuine bicategory: every tensor is a finite sum of elementary tensors, on which the coherence diagrams are checked, and the two sides of each diagram agree on all elements. No commutativity of the rings and no choice are used.

[Alphabeta Math, The Morita data satisfy the bicategory coherence axioms, Statement (lem-bimodule-tensor-associators-and-unitors-satisfy-bicategory-coherence)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-bimodule-tensor-associators-and-unitors-satisfy-bicategory-coherence)

```lean
theorem BimoduleTensorBicategoryCoherence :   let BimodStructure := fun (B A : RingCat.{u}) (M : AddCommGrpCat.{u}) =>
    Bimodule.{u,u,u}.1 B A M
  let Bimod := fun (B A : RingCat.{u}) => Sigma (BimodStructure B A)
  let sum := fun (T : AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (xs : List T) => List.sum xs
  let left := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} (M : Bimod B A) => M.2.1.smul
  let right := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} (M : Bimod B A) (a : A) =>
    M.2.2.val.smul (MulOpposite.op a)
  let Equivariant := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} (M N : Bimod B A) (f : M.1 → N.1) =>
    (∀ (b : B) (m : M.1), f (left M b m) = left N b (f m)) ∧
    (∀ (a : A) (m : M.1), f (right M a m) = right N a (f m))
  let Hom := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} (M N : Bimod B A) =>
    { f : AddMonoidHom M.1 N.1 // Equivariant M N f }
  let Iso := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} (M N : Bimod B A) =>
    { e : AddEquiv M.1 N.1 // Equivariant M N e }
  let isoHom := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} {M N : Bimod B A} (e : Iso M N) =>
    (⟨e.val.toAddMonoidHom, e.property⟩ : Hom M N)
  let idMap := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} (M : Bimod B A) =>
    (⟨AddMonoidHom.id M.1, ⟨fun _ _ => rfl, fun _ _ => rfl⟩⟩ : Hom M M)
  let comp := fun {B A : RingCat.{u}} {M N P : Bimod B A}
      (g : Hom N P) (f : Hom M N) =>
    (⟨g.val.comp f.val,
      ⟨fun b m => (congrArg g.val (f.property.1 b m)).trans (g.property.1 b (f.val m)),
       fun a m => (congrArg g.val (f.property.2 a m)).trans (g.property.2 a (f.val m))⟩⟩ :
      Hom M P)
  let regular := fun (A : RingCat.{u}) =>
    (⟨AddCommGrpCat.of A, (Bimodule.{u,u,u}.2.1 A).val⟩ : Bimod A A)
  let IsBalanced := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A)
      (T : AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (t : G.1 → F.1 → T) =>
    (∀ (g g' : G.1) (f : F.1), t (g + g') f = t g f + t g' f) ∧
    (∀ (g : G.1) (f f' : F.1), t g (f + f') = t g f + t g f') ∧
    (∀ (b : B) (g : G.1) (f : F.1), t (right G b g) f = t g (left F b f))
  let relation := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A)
      (x y : FreeAddGroup (Prod G.1 F.1)) =>
    let gen := fun (g : G.1) (f : F.1) => FreeAddGroup.of (g, f)
    (∃ p q : FreeAddGroup (Prod G.1 F.1), x = p + q ∧ y = q + p) ∨
    (∃ (g g' : G.1) (f : F.1), x = gen (g + g') f ∧ y = gen g f + gen g' f) ∨
    (∃ (g : G.1) (f f' : F.1), x = gen g (f + f') ∧ y = gen g f + gen g f') ∨
    (∃ (b : B) (g : G.1) (f : F.1), x = gen (right G b g) f ∧ y = gen g (left F b f))
  let congruence := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) =>
    addConGen (relation G F)
  let underlying := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) =>
    let c := congruence G F
    letI : AddCommGroup c.Quotient :=
      { AddCon.addGroup c with
        add_comm := fun x y => Quotient.inductionOn₂ x y fun p q =>
          Quotient.sound (s := c.toSetoid) (AddConGen.Rel.of _ _ (Or.inl ⟨p, q, rfl, rfl⟩)) }
    AddCommGrpCat.of c.Quotient
  let pure := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) (g : G.1) (f : F.1) =>
    (Quotient.mk (congruence G F).toSetoid (FreeAddGroup.of (g, f)) : underlying G F)
  ∃ (actions : ∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A),
        BimodStructure C A (underlying G F)),
    let tensor := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) =>
      (⟨underlying G F, actions G F⟩ : Bimod C A)
    let tmul := fun {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) =>
      (pure G F : G.1 → F.1 → (tensor G F).1)
    (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A),
      IsBalanced G F (tensor G F).1 (tmul G F) ∧
      ∀ (T : AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (b : G.1 → F.1 → T), IsBalanced G F T b →
        ∃! lift : AddMonoidHom (tensor G F).1 T, ∀ g f, lift (tmul G F g f) = b g f) ∧
    (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) (g : G.1) (f : F.1),
      (∀ c : C, left (tensor G F) c (tmul G F g f) = tmul G F (left G c g) f) ∧
      (∀ a : A, right (tensor G F) a (tmul G F g f) = tmul G F g (right F a f))) ∧
    ∃ (tensorMap : ∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} {G G' : Bimod C B} {F F' : Bimod B A},
        Hom G G' → Hom F F' → Hom (tensor G F) (tensor G' F'))
      (assoc : ∀ {D C B A : RingCat.{u}} (H : Bimod D C) (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A),
          Iso (tensor (tensor H G) F) (tensor H (tensor G F)))
      (leftUnitor : ∀ {B A : RingCat.{u}} (F : Bimod B A), Iso (tensor (regular B) F) F)
      (rightUnitor : ∀ {B A : RingCat.{u}} (F : Bimod B A), Iso (tensor F (regular A)) F),
      (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A) (x : (tensor G F).1),
        ∃ terms : List (Prod G.1 F.1),
          x = sum (tensor G F).1 (List.map (fun p => tmul G F p.1 p.2) terms)) ∧
      (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} {G G' : Bimod C B} {F F' : Bimod B A}
          (g : Hom G G') (f : Hom F F') (y : G.1) (x : F.1),
        (tensorMap g f).val (tmul G F y x) = tmul G' F' (g.val y) (f.val x)) ∧
      (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A),
        tensorMap (idMap G) (idMap F) = idMap (tensor G F)) ∧
      (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} {G G' G'' : Bimod C B} {F F' F'' : Bimod B A}
          (g : Hom G G') (g' : Hom G' G'') (f : Hom F F') (f' : Hom F' F''),
        tensorMap (comp g' g) (comp f' f) = comp (tensorMap g' f') (tensorMap g f)) ∧
      (∀ {D C B A : RingCat.{u}} (H : Bimod D C) (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A)
          (h : H.1) (g : G.1) (f : F.1),
        (assoc H G F).val (tmul (tensor H G) F (tmul H G h g) f) =
          tmul H (tensor G F) h (tmul G F g f)) ∧
      (∀ {B A : RingCat.{u}} (F : Bimod B A) (b : B) (a : A) (f : F.1),
        (leftUnitor F).val (tmul (regular B) F b f) = left F b f ∧
        (rightUnitor F).val (tmul F (regular A) f a) = right F a f) ∧
      (∀ {D C B A : RingCat.{u}} {H H' : Bimod D C} {G G' : Bimod C B} {F F' : Bimod B A}
          (h : Hom H H') (g : Hom G G') (f : Hom F F'),
        comp (isoHom (assoc H' G' F')) (tensorMap (tensorMap h g) f) =
          comp (tensorMap h (tensorMap g f)) (isoHom (assoc H G F))) ∧
      (∀ {B A : RingCat.{u}} {F F' : Bimod B A} (f : Hom F F'),
        comp (isoHom (leftUnitor F')) (tensorMap (idMap (regular B)) f) =
          comp f (isoHom (leftUnitor F)) ∧
        comp (isoHom (rightUnitor F')) (tensorMap f (idMap (regular A))) =
          comp f (isoHom (rightUnitor F))) ∧
      (∀ {E D C B A : RingCat.{u}}
          (K : Bimod E D) (H : Bimod D C) (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A),
        comp (isoHom (assoc K H (tensor G F))) (isoHom (assoc (tensor K H) G F)) =
          comp (tensorMap (idMap K) (isoHom (assoc H G F)))
            (comp (isoHom (assoc K (tensor H G) F))
              (tensorMap (isoHom (assoc K H G)) (idMap F)))) ∧
      (∀ {C B A : RingCat.{u}} (G : Bimod C B) (F : Bimod B A),
        comp (tensorMap (idMap G) (isoHom (leftUnitor F))) (isoHom (assoc G (regular B) F)) =
          tensorMap (isoHom (rightUnitor G)) (idMap F))
```

## EilenbergWatts: Eilenberg–Watts [1, 2]

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For unital rings \(R,S\), there is an equivalence from \(\Bimod(S,R)\)
to the category of additive, right-exact functors \(R\Mod\to S\Mod\)
that preserve all set-indexed coproducts, with natural transformations
as morphisms. It sends
\[
  B\longmapsto B\otimes_R-,\qquad f\longmapsto f\otimes_R\id .
\]
Its quasi-inverse sends \(F\) to \(F({}_R R)\) and \(\theta\) to
\(\theta_R\). For \(b\in F(R)\) and \(r\in R\), the right action is
\(br=F(\rho_r)(b)\), where \(\rho_r(x)=xr\). For composable bimodules
\(B\in\Bimod(S,R)\) and \(C\in\Bimod(T,S)\), composition corresponds to
\(C\otimes_S B\), and the identity corresponds to the regular bimodule.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 1.1 [thm:ew], p. 2](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

Let $A,B$ be unital rings. The assignment $M\mapsto T_M$ extends to an
schematic equivalence between the category of $(B,A)$-bimodules with
bimodule maps ([[def-bimodule]]) and the category of additive cocontinuous
functors $A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ with natural
transformations
([[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]]). It is full and
faithful with
$\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$,
naturally in $M$ and $M'$, and essentially surjective by
[[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]]; a quasi-inverse is
$F\mapsto F({}_AA)$. In particular $T_M\cong T_{M'}$ if and only if
$M\cong M'$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules. Categorical language has the schematic meaning of
[[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]; no category with proper-class
functors as set-coded objects is asserted. No commutativity and no choice are used.

[Alphabeta Math, Eilenberg-Watts is a schematic equivalence of Hom categories, Statement (cor-eilenberg-watts-is-an-equivalence-of-hom-categories)](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/cor-eilenberg-watts-is-an-equivalence-of-hom-categories)

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 1.1 (thm:ew), p. 2. The published PDF matches the project copy. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplies no correction for Theorem 1.1. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects

The statement is universe-polymorphic in the common ring universe and the module carrier universe. Coproduct preservation ranges over every index type in the module carrier universe. ULift places the regular module in that universe. Right exactness is preservation of finite colimits. The balanced universal property and elementary-tensor formulas specify the tensor assignments, the composition comparison and the regular-bimodule identity. The quasi-inverse, after forgetting its right actions, is evaluation at the regular module as a functor, so the formula also covers natural transformations. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem EilenbergWatts : let Mod := fun A : RingCat.{u} => ModuleCat.{max u v} A
let Actions := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) (M : Mod S) =>
  { d : Bimodule.1 S R M // d.1 = ModuleCat.isModule M }
let Bimod := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) => Sigma (Actions S R)
let right := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) (M : Bimod S R) (m : M.1) (r : R) =>
  letI : Module (MulOpposite R) M.1 := M.2.1.2.1
  MulOpposite.op r • m
let Hom := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) (M N : Bimod S R) =>
  { f : LinearMap (RingHom.id S) M.1 N.1 //
    ∀ (m : M.1) (r : R), f (right S R M m r) = right S R N (f m) r }
letI : ∀ S R : RingCat.{u}, CategoryTheory.Category (Bimod S R) := fun S R =>
  { Hom := Hom S R
    id := fun _ => ⟨LinearMap.id, fun _ _ => rfl⟩
    comp := fun f g =>
      ⟨LinearMap.comp g.val f.val, fun m r =>
        Eq.trans (congrArg (fun x => g.val x) (f.property m r))
          (g.property (f.val m) r)⟩
    id_comp := fun _ => Subtype.ext (LinearMap.id_comp _)
    comp_id := fun _ => Subtype.ext (LinearMap.comp_id _)
    assoc := fun _ _ _ => Subtype.ext (LinearMap.comp_assoc _ _ _) }
let forgetBimod : ∀ S R : RingCat.{u}, CategoryTheory.Functor (Bimod S R) (Mod S) :=
  fun _ _ =>
    { obj := fun M => M.1
      map := fun f => ModuleCat.ofHom f.val
      map_id := fun _ => rfl
      map_comp := fun _ _ => rfl }
let Good := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (Mod R) (Mod S)) =>
  CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F ∧
  CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
  ∀ I : Type (max u v), CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape
    (CategoryTheory.Discrete I) F
let PreservingFunctors := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) => CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (Good S R)
let incl := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) => CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι (Good S R)
let regular := fun (R : RingCat.{u}) => ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} R)
let rho : ∀ (R : RingCat.{u}), R → ModuleCat.Hom (regular R) (regular R) :=
  fun R r =>
    ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearEquiv.conjRingEquiv
      (LinearEquiv.symm (ULift.moduleEquiv : ULift.{v} R ≃ₗ[R] R)) (LinearMap.mulRight R r))
let eval := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) =>
  CategoryTheory.Functor.comp (incl S R)
    (CategoryTheory.Functor.obj (CategoryTheory.evaluation (Mod R) (Mod S)) (regular R))
let Balanced := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) (B : Bimod S R) (X : Mod R) (Y : Mod S)
    (p : B.1 → X → Y) =>
  (∀ (b b' : B.1) (x : X), p (b + b') x = p b x + p b' x) ∧
  (∀ (b : B.1) (x x' : X), p b (x + x') = p b x + p b x') ∧
  (∀ (s : S) (b : B.1) (x : X), p (s • b) x = s • p b x) ∧
  (∀ (r : R) (b : B.1) (x : X), p (right S R B b r) x = p b (r • x))
∃ EW : ∀ S R : RingCat.{u}, CategoryTheory.Equivalence (Bimod S R) (PreservingFunctors S R),
  let tensor := fun (S R : RingCat.{u}) (B : Bimod S R) =>
    CategoryTheory.Functor.obj (incl S R) ((EW S R).functor.obj B)
  ∃ pure : ∀ (S R : RingCat.{u}) (B : Bimod S R) (X : Mod R), B.1 → X → (tensor S R B).obj X,
    (∀ (S R : RingCat.{u}) (B : Bimod S R) (X : Mod R),
      Balanced S R B X ((tensor S R B).obj X) (pure S R B X) ∧
      ∀ (Y : Mod S) (p : B.1 → X → Y), Balanced S R B X Y p →
        ∃! f : LinearMap (RingHom.id S) ((tensor S R B).obj X) Y,
          ∀ (b : B.1) (x : X), f (pure S R B X b x) = p b x) ∧
    (∀ (S R : RingCat.{u}) (B : Bimod S R) (X Y : Mod R)
      (f : ModuleCat.Hom X Y) (b : B.1) (x : X),
      ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((tensor S R B).map f) (pure S R B X b x) =
        pure S R B Y b (ModuleCat.Hom.hom f x)) ∧
    (∀ (S R : RingCat.{u}) (B B' : Bimod S R) (f : Hom S R B B')
      (X : Mod R) (b : B.1) (x : X),
      ModuleCat.Hom.hom
        (CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app ((incl S R).map ((EW S R).functor.map f)) X)
        (pure S R B X b x) = pure S R B' X (f.val b) x) ∧
    (∀ S R : RingCat.{u},
      ∃ h : CategoryTheory.Functor.comp (EW S R).inverse (forgetBimod S R) = eval S R,
        ∀ (F : PreservingFunctors S R),
          let toEval := cast (congrArg ModuleCat.carrier (CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_obj h F))
          ∀ (m : ((EW S R).inverse.obj F).1) (r : R),
            toEval (right S R ((EW S R).inverse.obj F) m r) =
              ModuleCat.Hom.hom (F.obj.map (rho R r)) (toEval m)) ∧
    (∀ (T S R : RingCat.{u}) (C : Bimod T S) (B : Bimod S R),
      ∃ a : Actions T R ((tensor T S C).obj B.1),
        let CB : Bimod T R := ⟨(tensor T S C).obj B.1, a⟩
        (∀ (c : C.1) (b : B.1) (r : R),
          right T R CB (pure T S C B.1 c b) r = pure T S C B.1 c (right S R B b r)) ∧
        ∃ i : CategoryTheory.Iso (tensor T R CB)
            (CategoryTheory.Functor.comp (tensor S R B) (tensor T S C)),
          ∀ (X : Mod R) (c : C.1) (b : B.1) (x : X),
            ModuleCat.Hom.hom (i.hom.app X) (pure T R CB X (pure T S C B.1 c b) x) =
              pure T S C ((tensor S R B).obj X) c (pure S R B X b x)) ∧
    (∀ R : RingCat.{u}, ∃ a : Actions R R (regular R),
      let RR : Bimod R R := ⟨regular R, a⟩
      (∀ (x : ULift.{v} R) (r : R), right R R RR x r = ULift.up (x.down * r)) ∧
      ∃ i : CategoryTheory.Iso (tensor R R RR) (CategoryTheory.Functor.id (Mod R)),
        ∀ (X : Mod R) (r : ULift.{v} R) (x : X),
          ModuleCat.Hom.hom (i.hom.app X) (pure R R RR X r x) = r.down • x)
```

## ComplexEilenbergWatts: Complex-linear Eilenberg–Watts correspondence

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For \(\C\)-algebras the equivalence identifies bimodules with equal
scalar actions with \(\C\)-linear functors of the stated kind.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.1, unnumbered, p. 2](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.1, p. 2, unnumbered sentence immediately after Theorem 1.1. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The statement restricts the equivalence supplied by EilenbergWatts to the full subcategories of bimodules whose scalar actions agree through the two complex algebra maps and complex-linear functors. The target inherits additivity, right exactness and preservation of all set-indexed coproducts. The type was checked using the exact reviewed prerequisite statement as a hypothesis because its compiled proof module was unavailable.

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction for this endpoint was supplied in the task context. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ComplexEilenbergWatts : ∀ (S R : RingCat.{u}) [Algebra Complex S] [Algebra Complex R],
  let ew := Classical.choose _root_.EilenbergWatts S R
  let Bimod := Sigma (fun M : ModuleCat.{max u v} S =>
    { a : _root_.Bimodule.1 S R M // a.1 = ModuleCat.isModule M })
  let Good := fun F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (ModuleCat.{max u v} S) =>
    CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F ∧
    CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
    ∀ I : Type (max u v),
      CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape (CategoryTheory.Discrete I) F
  let GoodFunctors := CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory Good
  letI : CategoryTheory.Category.{max u v} Bimod :=
    (fun (c : CategoryTheory.Category.{max u v} Bimod)
      (_ : @CategoryTheory.Equivalence Bimod GoodFunctors c inferInstance) => c) _ ew
  let EqualScalars : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty Bimod := fun B =>
    letI : Module (MulOpposite R) B.1 := B.2.1.2.1
    ∀ (z : Complex) (b : B.1),
      algebraMap Complex S z • b = MulOpposite.op (algebraMap Complex R z) • b
  let ComplexLinear : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty GoodFunctors := fun F =>
    CategoryTheory.Functor.Linear Complex F.obj
  (∀ B : Bimod, EqualScalars B ↔ ComplexLinear (ew.functor.obj B)) ∧
  ∃ restricted : CategoryTheory.Equivalence
      (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory EqualScalars)
      (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory ComplexLinear),
    CategoryTheory.Functor.comp restricted.functor (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι ComplexLinear) =
      CategoryTheory.Functor.comp (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι EqualScalars) ew.functor
```

## SmallProjectiveGeneratorCorrespondence: Correspondence via small projective generators

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Let \(\mathcal A,\mathcal E\) be locally small abelian categories with
all set-indexed coproducts and small projective generators \(P,Q\).
Here small means that \(\Hom(P,-)\) or \(\Hom(Q,-)\) preserves those
coproducts. Put \(R=\End_{\mathcal A}(P)^\op\) and
\(S=\End_{\mathcal E}(Q)^\op\). The Hom functors give equivalences
\(\mathcal A\simeq R\Mod\) and \(\mathcal E\simeq S\Mod\)
[2, Chs.~8--10]. Theorem~1.1 then sends \(F\) to
\(\Hom_{\mathcal E}(Q,F(P))\), with actions
\[
 q^\op b p^\op=F(p)\circ b\circ q.
\]
A natural transformation acts by postcomposition with its component
at \(P\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.1, unnumbered, p. 2](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

All set-indexed coproducts range over the common hom universe, and the two category object universes are independent. The Hom equivalences use the canonical module-valued Hom functors. The correspondence uses the additive, right-exact, coproduct-preserving functors of Theorem 1.1. After forgetting the right action, it is evaluation at P followed by the Hom functor out of Q, with the displayed bimodule action and postcomposition formula stated explicitly. The registered prerequisites were available as translations.
```lean
theorem SmallProjectiveGeneratorCorrespondence : ∀ (A : Type u) (E : Type w)
    [CategoryTheory.Category.{v} A] [CategoryTheory.Category.{v} E]
    [CategoryTheory.Abelian A] [CategoryTheory.Abelian E]
    [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoproducts.{v} A]
    [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoproducts.{v} E]
    (P : A) (Q : E),
  CategoryTheory.Projective P →
  CategoryTheory.IsSeparator P →
  (∀ I : Type v, CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape
    (CategoryTheory.Discrete I)
    (CategoryTheory.Functor.obj CategoryTheory.preadditiveCoyoneda (Opposite.op P))) →
  CategoryTheory.Projective Q →
  CategoryTheory.IsSeparator Q →
  (∀ I : Type v, CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape
    (CategoryTheory.Discrete I)
    (CategoryTheory.Functor.obj CategoryTheory.preadditiveCoyoneda (Opposite.op Q))) →
  let R := MulOpposite (CategoryTheory.End P)
  let S := MulOpposite (CategoryTheory.End Q)
  let HP : CategoryTheory.Functor A (ModuleCat.{v} R) :=
    CategoryTheory.preadditiveCoyonedaObj P
  let HQ : CategoryTheory.Functor E (ModuleCat.{v} S) :=
    CategoryTheory.preadditiveCoyonedaObj Q
  let Good := fun F : CategoryTheory.Functor A E =>
    CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F ∧
      CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
      ∀ I : Type v, CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape
        (CategoryTheory.Discrete I) F
  let Functors := CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory Good
  let incl := CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι Good
  let eval := CategoryTheory.Functor.comp incl
    (CategoryTheory.Functor.comp
      (CategoryTheory.Functor.obj (CategoryTheory.evaluation A E) P) HQ)
  let Actions := fun (M : ModuleCat.{v} S) =>
    { d : Sigma (fun left : Module S M =>
        Subtype (fun right : Module (MulOpposite R) M =>
          letI : SMul S M := left.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
          letI : SMul (MulOpposite R) M :=
            right.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
          SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) S M)) //
      d.1 = ModuleCat.isModule M }
  let Bimod := Sigma Actions
  let right := fun (M : Bimod) (b : M.1) (r : R) =>
    letI : Module (MulOpposite R) M.1 := M.2.1.2.1
    MulOpposite.op r • b
  let Hom := fun (M N : Bimod) =>
    { f : LinearMap (RingHom.id S) M.1 N.1 //
      ∀ (b : M.1) (r : R), f (right M b r) = right N (f b) r }
  letI : CategoryTheory.Category Bimod :=
    { Hom := Hom
      id := fun _ => ⟨LinearMap.id, fun _ _ => rfl⟩
      comp := fun f g =>
        ⟨LinearMap.comp g.val f.val, fun b r =>
          Eq.trans (congrArg (fun x => g.val x) (f.property b r))
            (g.property (f.val b) r)⟩
      id_comp := fun _ => Subtype.ext (LinearMap.id_comp _)
      comp_id := fun _ => Subtype.ext (LinearMap.comp_id _)
      assoc := fun _ _ _ => Subtype.ext (LinearMap.comp_assoc _ _ _) }
  let forgetBimod : CategoryTheory.Functor Bimod (ModuleCat.{v} S) :=
    { obj := fun M => M.1
      map := fun f => ModuleCat.ofHom f.val
      map_id := fun _ => rfl
      map_comp := fun _ _ => rfl }
  CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence HP ∧
    CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence HQ ∧
    ∃ Φ : CategoryTheory.Equivalence Functors Bimod,
      ∃ h : CategoryTheory.Functor.comp Φ.functor forgetBimod = eval,
        let toHom := fun (F : Functors) =>
          cast (congrArg ModuleCat.carrier (CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_obj h F))
        (∀ (F : Functors) (b : (Φ.functor.obj F).1)
            (q : CategoryTheory.End Q) (p : CategoryTheory.End P),
          toHom F (MulOpposite.op q • right (Φ.functor.obj F) b (MulOpposite.op p)) =
            CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
              (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
                (CategoryTheory.End.asHom q) (toHom F b))
              (F.obj.map (CategoryTheory.End.asHom p))) ∧
        (∀ (F G : Functors) (θ : Quiver.Hom F G) (b : (Φ.functor.obj F).1),
          toHom G ((Φ.functor.map θ).val b) =
            CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (toHom F b)
              (CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app (incl.map θ) P))
```

## ConjugationEmbeddingCentralizerCoset: Conjugation embeddings and their centralizer cosets

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.2, unnumbered, p. 2](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

```lean
theorem ConjugationEmbeddingCentralizerCoset : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (H G : Subgroup U) (α β : U)
  (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
  (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
  MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex
      (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα).toHom =
    MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex
      (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ).toHom ↔
  LeftCosetEquivalence (Subgroup.centralizer (H : Set U) : Set U) α β
```

## InductionRestrictionBimoduleStrands: Induction and restriction bimodule strands

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

The up and down strands below denote
\[
 \I_{\co\alpha}^{G,H}={}_{\C[G]}(\C[G])_{\alpha_*,\C[H]},\qquad
 \D_{\co\alpha}^{H,G}={}_{\C[H],\alpha_*}(\C[G])_{\C[G]}.
\]
The actions are \(x\cdot h=x\alpha h\alpha^{-1}\) on \(\I\) and
\(h\cdot x=\alpha h\alpha^{-1}x\) on \(\D\). Tensoring on the right
gives induction and restriction, respectively. The target group
is on the left. Read horizontal composition as tensor product over
the middle group and vertical composition from bottom to top.

```lean
theorem InductionRestrictionBimoduleStrands : ∀ {U : Type u} [Group U],
  (∀ (H G : Subgroup U) (α : U) (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G),
    let A := MonoidAlgebra Complex H
    let B := MonoidAlgebra Complex G
    let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
    let φ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex a.toHom
    let up := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a
    let down := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down a
    let Ind : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) :=
      CategoryTheory.Functor.comp
        (CategoryTheory.Functor.comp
          (Rep.ofModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := Complex) (G := H))
          (Rep.indFunctor Complex a.toHom))
        (Rep.toModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := Complex) (G := G))
    let Res : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :=
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ.toRingHom
    let TensorsOnRight := fun (S R : Type u) [Ring S] [Ring R]
        (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N]
        (left : S → N → N) (right : R → N → N)
        (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (ModuleCat.{max u v} S)) =>
      let Balanced := fun (X : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (Y : ModuleCat.{max u v} S)
          (p : N → X → Y) =>
        (∀ n n' : N, ∀ x : X, p (n + n') x = p n x + p n' x) ∧
        (∀ n : N, ∀ x x' : X, p n (x + x') = p n x + p n x') ∧
        (∀ (s : S) (n : N) (x : X), p (left s n) x = s • p n x) ∧
        (∀ (r : R) (n : N) (x : X), p (right r n) x = p n (r • x))
      ∃ τ : ∀ X : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, N → X → F.obj X,
        (∀ X, Balanced X (F.obj X) (τ X)) ∧
        (∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (Y : ModuleCat.{max u v} S)
            (p : N → X → Y), Balanced X Y p →
          ∃! f : LinearMap (RingHom.id S) (F.obj X) Y,
            ∀ (n : N) (x : X), f (τ X n x) = p n x) ∧
        (∀ (X Y : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (f : Quiver.Hom X Y) (n : N) (x : X),
          ModuleCat.Hom.hom (F.map f) (τ X n x) = τ Y n (ModuleCat.Hom.hom f x))
    (∀ (h : H) (c : Complex),
      φ (MonoidAlgebra.single h c) = MonoidAlgebra.single (a.toHom h) c) ∧
    (∀ (β : U) (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
      φ = MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex
        (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ).toHom ↔
      LeftCosetEquivalence (Subgroup.centralizer (H : Set U) : Set U) α β) ∧
    ∃ (I : Bimodule.1 B A (MonoidAlgebra Complex up.basis.carrier))
      (D : Bimodule.1 A B (MonoidAlgebra Complex down.basis.carrier)),
      let leftI := @SMul.smul B B I.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
      let rightI := fun (r : A) (x : B) =>
        @SMul.smul (MulOpposite A) B
          I.2.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul (MulOpposite.op r) x
      let leftD := @SMul.smul A B D.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul
      let rightD := fun (r : B) (x : B) =>
        @SMul.smul (MulOpposite B) B
          D.2.1.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSemigroupAction.toSMul (MulOpposite.op r) x
      (∀ (s x : B), leftI s x = s * x) ∧
      (∀ (r : A) (x : B), rightI r x = x * φ r) ∧
      (∀ (r : A) (x : B), leftD r x = φ r * x) ∧
      (∀ (s x : B), rightD s x = x * s) ∧
      (∀ (g : G) (h : H) (x : B),
        MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff
          (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.actLinear Complex up.basis (g, h⁻¹) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x)) =
        leftI (MonoidAlgebra.single g 1) (rightI (MonoidAlgebra.single h 1) x)) ∧
      (∀ (h : H) (g : G) (x : B),
        MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff
          (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.actLinear Complex down.basis (h, g⁻¹) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x)) =
        leftD (MonoidAlgebra.single h 1) (rightD (MonoidAlgebra.single g 1) x)) ∧
      TensorsOnRight B A B leftI rightI Ind ∧
      TensorsOnRight A B B leftD rightD Res) ∧
  (∀ (K L J : Subgroup U) (p : MackeyDiagrams.Word K L) (q : MackeyDiagrams.Word L J),
    let X := Finsupp p.basis.carrier Complex
    let Y := Finsupp q.basis.carrier Complex
    let Z := Finsupp (MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor p q).basis.carrier Complex
    let right := fun (r : MonoidAlgebra Complex L) (x : X) =>
      MackeyDiagrams.freeLift Complex
        (fun h : L => MackeyDiagrams.Biset.actLinear Complex p.basis (1, h⁻¹) x)
        (MonoidAlgebra.coeff r)
    let left := fun (r : MonoidAlgebra Complex L) (y : Y) =>
      MackeyDiagrams.freeLift Complex
        (fun h : L => MackeyDiagrams.Biset.actLinear Complex q.basis (h, 1) y)
        (MonoidAlgebra.coeff r)
    let pair := MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pairLinear Complex p.basis q.basis
    (∀ (r : MonoidAlgebra Complex L) (x : X) (y : Y),
      pair (right r x) y = pair x (left r y)) ∧
    (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module Complex M]
        (f : LinearMap (RingHom.id Complex) X (LinearMap (RingHom.id Complex) Y M)),
      (∀ (r : MonoidAlgebra Complex L) (x : X) (y : Y),
        f (right r x) y = f x (left r y)) →
      ∃! lift : LinearMap (RingHom.id Complex) Z M,
        ∀ (x : X) (y : Y), lift (pair x y) = f x y)) ∧
  (∀ (K L J : Subgroup U)
      (p p' : MackeyDiagrams.Word K L) (q q' : MackeyDiagrams.Word L J)
      (d : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex p p')
      (e : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex q q')
      (x : Finsupp p.basis.carrier Complex) (y : Finsupp q.basis.carrier Complex),
    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal d e)).eval.toLinearMap
      (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pairLinear Complex p.basis q.basis x y) =
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pairLinear Complex p'.basis q'.basis
      ((MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret d).eval.toLinearMap x)
      ((MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret e).eval.toLinearMap y)) ∧
  (∀ (K H : Subgroup U) (p q r : MackeyDiagrams.Word K H)
      (bottom : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex p q)
      (top : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex q r),
    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical bottom top)).eval.toLinearMap =
      LinearMap.comp (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret top).eval.toLinearMap
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret bottom).eval.toLinearMap)
```

## GroupElementDotCriterion: Admissible dots and their evaluated maps

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

Let \(\co\alpha,\co\beta\) be two labels for embeddings of \(H\) into
\(G\). Choose \(\alpha'\in\co\alpha\) and \(\beta'\in\co\beta\) with
\(d=\alpha'(\beta')^{-1}\in G\). This determines a node
\[
 \I_{\co\alpha}^{G,H}\xrightarrow{\ \cdot d\ }\I_{\co\beta}^{G,H},
 \qquad x\longmapsto xd.
\]
The map respects the right action exactly when
\(\alpha_*(h)d=d\beta_*(h)\) for all \(h\in H\).
The possible group elements are \(G\cap\alpha C_U(H)\beta^{-1}\).
Changing representatives can change \(d\) and hence the map.
For the down strands the same \(d\) gives \(x\mapsto d^{-1}x\).

```lean
theorem GroupElementDotCriterion : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (H G : Subgroup U) (α β : U)
  (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
  (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
  let A := MonoidAlgebra Complex H
  let B := MonoidAlgebra Complex G
  let C := (Subgroup.centralizer (H : Set U) : Set U)
  let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ
  let φ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a)
  let ψ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b)
  let up := fun t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.upDot (R := Complex) t)
  let down := fun t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.downDot (R := Complex) t)
  (φ = ψ ↔ LeftCosetEquivalence C α β) ∧
  (∀ d : G,
    let rightMul := fun x : B => x * MonoidAlgebra.single d 1
    let intertwines := ∀ h : H,
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a h * d = d * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b h
    ((∀ (x : B) (r : A), rightMul (x * φ r) = rightMul x * ψ r) ↔ intertwines) ∧
    (intertwines ↔ (d : U) ∈ Set.image (fun c : U => α * c * β⁻¹) C) ∧
    (intertwines ↔ ∃ α' β' : U, LeftCosetEquivalence C α α' ∧
      LeftCosetEquivalence C β β' ∧ (d : U) = α' * (β')⁻¹) ∧
    (intertwines ↔ ∃ t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b, MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t = d)) ∧
  (∀ (t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b) (x : B),
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (up t) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) =
      MonoidAlgebra.coeff (x * MonoidAlgebra.single (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t) 1) ∧
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (down t) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) =
      MonoidAlgebra.coeff (MonoidAlgebra.single (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t)⁻¹ 1 * x)) ∧
  (∀ t s : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b,
    let sameElement := MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t = MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element s
    (up t = up s ↔ sameElement) ∧ (down t = down s ↔ sameElement))
```

## InductionRestrictionAdjunction: Induction left adjoint to restriction

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

The up and down strands below denote
\[
 \I_{\co\alpha}^{G,H}={}_{\C[G]}(\C[G])_{\alpha_*,\C[H]},\qquad
 \D_{\co\alpha}^{H,G}={}_{\C[H],\alpha_*}(\C[G])_{\C[G]}.
\]
The actions are \(x\cdot h=x\alpha h\alpha^{-1}\) on \(\I\) and
\(h\cdot x=\alpha h\alpha^{-1}x\) on \(\D\). Tensoring on the right
gives induction and restriction, respectively. The target group
is on the left. Read horizontal composition as tensor product over
the middle group and vertical composition from bottom to top.

Suppress the embedding and group labels on \(\I,\D\).
Each tensor product is over the group algebra of the middle region.
For \(\Ind_{\alpha_*}\dashv\Res_{\alpha_*}\), the unit and counit are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
   \eta &: \C[H]\longrightarrow \D\otimes_{\C[G]}\I,\qquad
      h\longmapsto \alpha_*(h)\otimes 1,\\
   \ev &: \I\otimes_{\C[H]}\D\longrightarrow \C[G],\qquad
      x\otimes y\longmapsto xy.
 \end{aligned}
\]
In the unit formula, \(\D\otimes_{\C[G]}\I\) identifies with \(\C[G]\) by multiplication.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 1.2, Cups and caps, pp. 3–4, https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the project TikZ fixes the ordinary cup at the empty H boundary and the multiplication cap at the empty G boundary. The defect report at https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects returned HTTP 404. The task context supplies no correction for this endpoint. The type uses complex group algebras and the conjugation embedding of InductionRestrictionBimoduleStrands at arbitrary index. It gives the two typed diagram evaluations, the multiplication identification for the cup target, and their correspondence with the adjunction components on module tensors. The tensor generator uses the inverse group index because Mathlib induction acts on its basis coordinate by right multiplication by the inverse. The Lean type elaborated through the shared compilation slot. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem InductionRestrictionAdjunction : ∀ {U : Type u} [Group U] (H G : Subgroup U) (α : U)
    (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G),
  let A := MonoidAlgebra Complex H
  let B := MonoidAlgebra Complex G
  let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let φ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex a.toHom
  let up := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a
  let down := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down a
  let downUp := MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor down up
  let cup := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.ordinaryCup (R := Complex) a)
  let cap := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.multiplicationCap (R := Complex) a)
  let pairDI := fun (x y : B) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pairLinear Complex down.basis up.basis
      (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff y)
  let pairID := fun (x y : B) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pairLinear Complex up.basis down.basis
      (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff y)
  let toRep : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (Rep.{max u v} Complex H) :=
    Rep.ofModuleMonoidAlgebra
  let Ind : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) :=
    CategoryTheory.Functor.comp
      (CategoryTheory.Functor.comp toRep (Rep.indFunctor Complex a.toHom))
      (Rep.toModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := Complex) (G := G))
  let Res : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B) (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :=
    ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ.toRingHom
  let pure := fun (X : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (b : B) (x : X) =>
    let ρ := Rep.ρ (toRep.obj X)
    show Ind.obj X from
      (Representation.asModuleEquiv (Representation.ind a.toHom ρ)).symm
        (MackeyDiagrams.freeLift Complex
          (fun g : G => Representation.IndV.mk a.toHom ρ g⁻¹ x) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff b))
  (∀ h : A, cup.toLinearMap (MonoidAlgebra.coeff h) = pairDI (φ h) 1) ∧
  (∀ x y : B, cap.toLinearMap (pairID x y) = MonoidAlgebra.coeff (x * y)) ∧
  ∃ m : LinearEquiv (RingHom.id Complex) (Finsupp downUp.basis.carrier Complex) B,
    (∀ x y : B, m (pairDI x y) = x * y) ∧
    (∀ (k l : H) (z : Finsupp downUp.basis.carrier Complex),
      m (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.actLinear Complex downUp.basis (k, l⁻¹) z) =
        φ (MonoidAlgebra.single k 1) * m z * φ (MonoidAlgebra.single l 1)) ∧
    ∃ adj : CategoryTheory.Adjunction Ind Res,
      (∀ (X : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (h : A) (x : X),
        ModuleCat.Hom.hom (adj.unit.app X) (h • x) =
          pure X (m (cup.toLinearMap (MonoidAlgebra.coeff h))) x) ∧
      (∀ (Y : ModuleCat.{max u v} B) (x y : B) (z : Y),
        ModuleCat.Hom.hom (adj.counit.app Y) (pure (Res.obj Y) x (y • z)) =
          (MonoidAlgebra.ofCoeff (cap.toLinearMap (pairID x y)) : B) • z)
```
