## CurlAcrossTrivalentVertex: Moving a scalar right curl across a merge or split

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

A right curl with no dot multiplies by its index. It can move
across a merge or split if the new curl has the same index.
The right input and the merged strand have the same right
region \(K\). The left input has right region \(H\), where
\[
 [H:\cg{\alpha}{L}]=[H:\cg{\alpha}{K}]\,[K:L]
\]
for \(L\le K\) and finite indices.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.2, Moving a curl across a vertex, p. 9](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.2, “Moving a curl across a vertex,” p. 9. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The right branch and the merged up-strand both have right region K and have the same index when they use the same loop. The left branch has right region H. For L ≤ K, the subgroup-index formula uses the images of L and K under conjugation by α. The statement compares the complex-linear evaluations for both placements across the induction merge and split when the finite indices agree. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The owner’s 27 November 2026 clarification in input.request, recorded at 2026-11-27T04:57:54.839065+00:00 in evidence/language-audit-20261127/owner-clarification.json, requires preserving the two mixed junctions shown for the undotted right curl in (4.1). The record supplies no separate request ID. The drawing composes upToUpDown with upDownToUp and is undotted as specified in § 3.2. Lean checked the proposition and confirmed that the curl has exactly these two planar events.

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. Any correction to this endpoint remains unverified. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem CurlAcrossTrivalentVertex : ∀ {U : Type u} [Group U] (K H G : Subgroup U) (γ α : U)
    (hγ : ∀ h : H, γ * (h : U) * γ⁻¹ ∈ G)
    (hα : ∀ k : K, α * (k : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ H),
  let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator γ hγ
  let ba := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp b a
  let leftStrand := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up b
  let rightStrand := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a
  let mergedStrand := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up ba
  let leftId := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) leftStrand)
  let rightId := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) rightStrand)
  let mergedId := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) mergedStrand)
  let merge := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
    (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp b a)
  let split := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
    (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.splitUp b a)
  let rightCurl := fun {A B M : Subgroup U}
      (strand : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A B)
      (loop : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding M A)
      (finite : Subgroup.FiniteIndex (MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom loop))) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
        (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.upToUpDown strand loop finite))
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent
        (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.upDownToUp strand loop))
  let evalDrawing := fun {A B : Subgroup U} {p q : MackeyDiagrams.Word A B}
      (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex p q) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret drawing)
  (∀ (L : Subgroup U), L ≤ K →
    let inK := Subgroup.subgroupOf L K
    let imageK := MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a)
    let imageL := Subgroup.map (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a) inK
    Subgroup.FiniteIndex inK → Subgroup.FiniteIndex imageK → Subgroup.FiniteIndex imageL →
      Subgroup.index imageL = Subgroup.index imageK * Subgroup.relIndex L K) ∧
  (∀ (M : Subgroup U) (mergedLoop : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding M K),
    let mergedImage := MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom mergedLoop)
    ∀ (finiteMerged : Subgroup.FiniteIndex mergedImage),
      let mergedIndex := Subgroup.index mergedImage
      let curlMerged := rightCurl ba mergedLoop finiteMerged
      evalDrawing curlMerged =
        evalDrawing
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (mergedIndex : Complex) mergedId) ∧
      (∀ (N : Subgroup U) (rightLoop : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding N K),
        let rightImage := MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom rightLoop)
        ∀ (finiteRight : Subgroup.FiniteIndex rightImage),
          let rightIndex := Subgroup.index rightImage
          let curlRight := rightCurl a rightLoop finiteRight
          let curlOnRight := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal leftId curlRight
          evalDrawing curlRight =
            evalDrawing
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (rightIndex : Complex) rightId) ∧
          (rightIndex = mergedIndex →
            evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical curlOnRight merge) =
              evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical merge curlMerged) ∧
            evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical split curlOnRight) =
              evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical curlMerged split))) ∧
      (∀ (N : Subgroup U) (leftLoop : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding N H),
        let leftImage := MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom leftLoop)
        ∀ (finiteLeft : Subgroup.FiniteIndex leftImage),
          let leftIndex := Subgroup.index leftImage
          let curlLeft := rightCurl b leftLoop finiteLeft
          let curlOnLeft := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal curlLeft rightId
          evalDrawing curlLeft =
            evalDrawing
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (leftIndex : Complex) leftId) ∧
          (leftIndex = mergedIndex →
            evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical curlOnLeft merge) =
              evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical merge curlMerged) ∧
            evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical split curlOnLeft) =
              evalDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical curlMerged split))))
```

## DifferentCurlIndices: Two curls with different indices

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For \(G=H=C_2\) and \(K=L=1\),
the curls using \(1\) multiply by \(1\) on the right input and
by \(2\) on the left.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.1 [ex:different-curl-indices], p. 9](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.1 [ex:different-curl-indices], p. 9. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The multiplicative group of ZMod 2 realizes C₂. Its top subgroup serves as both G and H, and its trivial subgroup serves as both K and L. Both diagrams are right curls on upward strands with the trivial loop group. The right input has right region K and coefficient 1. The left input has right region H and coefficient 2. Both scalar identities are over Complex. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction for this endpoint was available in the supplied context. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem DifferentCurlIndices : let U := Multiplicative (ZMod 2)
let G : Subgroup U := ⊤
let H := G
let K : Subgroup U := ⊥
let L := K
let leftStrand := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator (H := H) (G := G) (1 : U)
  (fun _ => by simp [G])
let rightStrand := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator (H := K) (G := H) (1 : U)
  (fun _ => by simp [H, G])
let rightLoop := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.id L
let leftLoop := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator (H := L) (G := H) (1 : U)
  (fun _ => by simp [H, G])
let rightCurl := fun {A B M : Subgroup U}
    (strand : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A B)
    (loop : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding M A)
    (finite : Subgroup.FiniteIndex (MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom loop))) =>
  let up := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up strand
  let loopUp := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up loop
  let loopDown := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down loop
  let straight := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) up
  let cup := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal straight
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.reverseCup loop finite)
  let throughCurl := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.mergeUp strand loop)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.splitUp strand loop))
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id loopDown)
  let cap := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal straight
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.multiplicationCap loop)
  MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.insertRightUnit up)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical cup
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate up loopUp loopDown)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical throughCurl
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate up loopUp loopDown)
            (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical cap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.rightUnit up))))))
MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (rightCurl rightStrand rightLoop inferInstance) =
  MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.scale (1 : Complex)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up rightStrand))) ∧
MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (rightCurl leftStrand leftLoop inferInstance) =
  MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.scale (2 : Complex)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up leftStrand)))
```

## LeftDownReidemeisterCurl: Left curl on a down-strand

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Use \(K\xrightarrow{\delta_*}H\xrightarrow{\alpha_*}G\).
The subscript on \(\id\) lists the groups on the left and right.

\[
\text{left curl on a down-strand}   =
       [H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\,\id_{H\cdot G}
\]

The \(K\)-loops require finite \([H:\cg{\delta}{K}]\).

```latex
\usetikzlibrary{arrows.meta,decorations.markings}

\newcommand{\C}{\mathbb C}
\newcommand{\Mod}{\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}}

  wire/.style={line width=.9pt,line cap=round},
  oriented/.style={wire,decoration={markings,mark=at position .57 with {\arrow{Stealth[length=5pt,width=5pt]}}},postaction={decorate}},
  region/.style={font=\normalsize,inner sep=1.5pt,outer sep=0pt},
  strandlabel/.style={font=\normalsize,inner sep=1.5pt,outer sep=0pt}
}

\newcommand{\reidemeistercurl}[8]{%
 \begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,baseline=-.61cm]
   \useasboundingbox (-2.13,-1.07) rectangle (2.13,.85);
   \draw[#2] (0,-.76)--(0,.76);

     \draw[#3] (0,.27)
       .. controls (.34,.36) and (.71,.62) .. (.95,.45)
       .. controls (1.20,.27) and (1.17,-.24) .. (.98,-.42)
       .. controls (.71,-.67) and (.30,-.36) .. (0,-.27);
```

## NormalizedIndexValuedReidemeisterCurls: Normalized index-valued Reidemeister curls

Use \(K\xrightarrow{\delta_*}H\xrightarrow{\alpha_*}G\).

```lean
theorem NormalizedTrivalentCurl : ∀ {U : Type u} [Group U] (K H G : Subgroup U) (γ α : U)
    (hγ : ∀ h : H, γ * (h : U) * γ⁻¹ ∈ G)
    (hα : ∀ k : K, α * (k : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ H),
  let left := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator γ hγ
  let right := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let merged := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp left right
  let normalizes := fun {A B : Subgroup U} (strand : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A B) =>
    ∀ (M : Subgroup U) (loop : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding M A),
      let image := MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom loop)
      ∀ finite : Subgroup.FiniteIndex image,
        let curl := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
            (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.upToUpDown strand loop finite))
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent
            (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.upDownToUp strand loop))
        let straight := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up strand))
        MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale ((Subgroup.index image : Complex)⁻¹) curl)) =
          MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret straight)
  normalizes left ∧ normalizes right ∧ normalizes merged
```

## FixedBoundaryReplacementPreorder: Preorder on shapes at fixed boundary

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For shapes \(A,B\) with the same boundary shape, write \(A\preceq B\)
if every labelling of \(A\) can be replaced by a labelling of \(B\)
with the same boundary groups, boundary cosets, and map. Internal
labels may change. This is inclusion of the sets of maps at each
fixed boundary, so the relation is reflexive and transitive.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.3, unnumbered, p. 10](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

Translation source: article. The unnumbered statement in Ian Xiao's Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, §3.3, p. 10, gives inclusion of attainable maps at each fixed boundary, reflexivity, and transitivity for shapes with the same boundary shape. The published PDF matches the project copy. Shapes share ordered bottom and top orientations. The full typed labelling fiber fixes the boundary groups and strand cosets, permits internal labels to vary, and evaluates the stored drawing. The owner clarification of 27 November 2026 in input.request applies the same finite complex linear label convention to every dot. Each term is an eligible group element, and a group-element dot is the coefficient-one singleton. The mark remains part of the shape. The designated defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, so its contents could not be reviewed. The supplied context contains no statement correction for this endpoint. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf#page=10 https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ShapeReplaces s t ↔
      ∀ (A B : Subgroup U) (p q : MackeyDiagrams.Boundary A B),
        MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.attainable
          (fun v (label : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary Complex p q v) => MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary.interpret label) (Subtype.val s) ⊆
        MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.attainable
          (fun v (label : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary Complex p q v) => MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary.interpret label) (Subtype.val t)) ∧
  (∀ s : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.Shapes (U := U) Complex boundary,
```

## RightInputDotSlideObstruction: A dot that cannot move to the right input

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Take the standard inclusions in the finitary symmetric group
\[
   K=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2\})\ \le\
   H=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3\})\ \le\
   G=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3,4\}).
\]
Fix all boundary strands to be these inclusions and their composite.
Put \(g=(3\,4)\) on the merged strand of \(B\). It centralizes
\(K\), so \(g,1\) represent the same label there. The map sends
\(1\otimes1\) to \(g\). In shape \(A\), the image of \(1\otimes1\)
is the right-input label and lies in \(H\), whereas \(g\notin H\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.2 [ex:dot-slide-obstruction], p. 10](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.3, Example 3.2 [ex:dot-slide-obstruction], p. 10. Proposition 3.2 specifies the two induction-merge shapes. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the author's HTML reproduces the example. Lean uses zero-based points in Fin 4, so Equiv.swap 2 3 represents the paper's (3 4). https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams#ex:dot-slide-obstruction

The 27 November 2026 owner clarification in input.request applies to both marks. B uses the coefficient-one singleton at (3 4), and A ranges over every finite complex linear label of termwise eligible elements. Its value at 1 ⊗ 1 is the embedded label in ℂ[G], supported in H. The clarification governs the Lean dot language.

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction for Example 3.2 was available. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem RightInputDotSlideObstruction : let U := Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)
let G : Subgroup U := ⊤
let H := MulAction.stabilizer U (3 : Fin 4)
let K := H ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer U (2 : Fin 4)
let inG : ∀ x : U, x ∈ G := fun _ => Subgroup.mem_top _
let α : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (by
    intro k
    simpa only [one_mul, inv_one, mul_one] using (inf_le_left : K ≤ H) k.property)
let γ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (fun _ => inG _)
let target := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp γ α
let g : G := ⟨Equiv.swap (2 : Fin 4) 3, inG _⟩
let gLabel : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K G :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator (g : U) (fun _ => inG _)
let input := MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up γ)
  (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up α)
let output := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up target
let unitTensor := Finsupp.single
  (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction γ)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction α) 1 1) (1 : Complex)
(g : U) ∈ Subgroup.centralizer (K : Set U) ∧ gLabel = target ∧ (g : U) ∉ H ∧
  ∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Dot target target, MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element d = g ∧
    let B : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex input output :=
      MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent
          (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp γ α))
        (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
          (Finsupp.single d (1 : Complex) : MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex target target))
    let evalB := MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret B)
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap evalB unitTensor = Finsupp.single g 1 ∧
      ∀ (β : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H) (label : MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex α β)
        (h : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp γ β = target),
        let A : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex input
            (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp γ β)) :=
          MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
                (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up γ)))
              (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing label))
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent
              (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp γ β))
        let evalA := MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret
            (Eq.ndrec (motive := fun out =>
              MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex input (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up out)) A h))
        let imageA := MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap evalA unitTensor
        imageA = Finsupp.mapDomain
          (fun term => MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom γ (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element term))
          label ∧
        (∀ x : G, x ∈ Finsupp.support imageA → (x : U) ∈ H) ∧
        evalA ≠ evalB
```

## DotSlidePreorderNotSymmetric: The dot-slide preorder is not symmetric

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For shapes \(A,B\) with the same boundary shape, write \(A\preceq B\)
if every labelling of \(A\) can be replaced by a labelling of \(B\)
with the same boundary groups, boundary cosets, and map. Internal
labels may change. This is inclusion of the sets of maps at each
fixed boundary, so the relation is reflexive and transitive.

Let \(A\) be the induction merge with a dot on the right input, and
let \(B\) be the induction merge with a dot on the merged strand. Then
\(A\preceq B\) and \(B\npreceq A\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 3.2 [prop:preorder-not-symmetric], p. 10](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, §3.3, Proposition 3.2 [prop:preorder-not-symmetric], p. 10. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. Forward replacement holds for every ambient group. Example 3.2 places the standard inclusions in the finitary symmetric group and takes S₄ as the outer boundary group G. For the reverse failure, Lean uses the finite realization with Equiv.Perm (Fin 4) as ambient group and its top subgroup as G, with the same boundary inclusions and composite. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf#page=10

The owner clarification of 27 November 2026, recorded in translation recheck request f13b4bd8ba9fe139, gives every marked vertex a finite complex linear combination of termwise eligible group elements. A group-element dot is the coefficient-one singleton. The identity-labelled drawings witness the two shapes at the ordered boundary of two upward inputs and one upward output. ShapeReplaces ranges over the full PlanarAtBoundary fibers at fixed boundary groups and strand cosets and compares the evaluations of the stored diagrams. InductionMergeDotSlide supplies the forward slide term by term. RightInputDotSlideObstruction records that every supported term of a right-input label maps into the embedded H and that the coefficient-one trunk label is supported at (3 4), which lies outside H.

The designated article defect report returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction to the statement of Proposition 3.2 was available. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem DotSlidePreorderNotSymmetric : let boundary : List Bool × List Bool := ([true, true], [true])
let S4 := Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)
let G : Subgroup S4 := ⊤
let H := MulAction.stabilizer S4 (3 : Fin 4)
let K := H ⊓ MulAction.stabilizer S4 (2 : Fin 4)
let left : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (fun _ => Subgroup.mem_top _)
let right : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (by
    intro k
    simpa only [one_mul, inv_one, mul_one] using
      (inf_le_left : K ≤ H) (Subtype.property k))
let leftWire := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
  (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up left))
let merge := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
  (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp left right)
let rightDot := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
  (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.identity (R := Complex) right)
let trunkDot := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
  (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.identity (R := Complex)
    (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp left right))
let rightMarked := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
  (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal leftWire rightDot) merge
let trunkMarked := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical merge trunkDot
let A₄ : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.Shapes (U := S4) Complex boundary :=
  ⟨MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.planarShape rightMarked, ⟨G, K, _, _, rightMarked, rfl, rfl⟩⟩
let B₄ : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.Shapes (U := S4) Complex boundary :=
  ⟨MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.planarShape trunkMarked, ⟨G, K, _, _, trunkMarked, rfl, rfl⟩⟩
(∀ {U : Type*} [Group U],
  let T : Subgroup U := ⊤
  let embedding := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.id T
  let wire := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up embedding))
  let merge := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent (R := Complex)
    (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp embedding embedding)
  let rightDot := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
    (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.identity (R := Complex) embedding)
  let trunkDot := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
    (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.identity (R := Complex)
      (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp embedding embedding))
  let rightMarked := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal wire rightDot) merge
  let trunkMarked := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical merge trunkDot
  let A : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.Shapes (U := U) Complex boundary :=
```

## InductionBimoduleOrbitSumBasis: Orbit-sum basis for induction-bimodule maps

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Fix a group \(U\). For \(X\le U\), write \(\C[X]\) for its complex group algebra.
If \(\cg{\alpha}{H}=\alpha H\alpha^{-1}\le G\), write
\(\alpha_*:\C[H]\to \C[G]\) for conjugation by \(\alpha\), extended linearly.
This map depends exactly on
\[
 \bar\alpha=\alpha C_U(H),\qquad
 C_U(H)=\{u\in U:uh=hu\text{ for all }h\in H\}.
\]
The centralizer in a strand label is taken for the source of its
embedding.

The up and down strands below denote
\[
 \I_{\co\alpha}^{G,H}={}_{\C[G]}(\C[G])_{\alpha_*,\C[H]},\qquad
 \D_{\co\alpha}^{H,G}={}_{\C[H],\alpha_*}(\C[G])_{\C[G]}.
\]
The actions are \(x\cdot h=x\alpha h\alpha^{-1}\) on \(\I\) and
\(h\cdot x=\alpha h\alpha^{-1}x\) on \(\D\). Tensoring on the right
gives induction and restriction, respectively. The target group
is on the left. Read horizontal composition as tensor product over
the middle group and vertical composition from bottom to top.

The space of bimodule maps from \(\I_{\bar\alpha}^{G,H}\) to
\(\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\) has a basis given by right multiplication
by the sums of the finite orbits of
\[
       h\cdot g=\alpha_*(h)g\,\beta_*(h)^{-1}
       \qquad(h\in H,\ g\in G).
\]
The single group-element dots are the singleton orbits. If \(H\) is
finite, the sum over each orbit is realized by a diagram.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 3.3 [prop:orbit-hom], p. 10](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the proposition agrees with the project TeX and the author's HTML. The Lean basis is indexed by the distinct finite orbit sets, and the realization clause uses the typed upward induction boundary. The supplied defect report returned HTTP 404, and the task context supplies no statement correction for this endpoint. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem InductionBimoduleOrbitSumBasis : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (H G : Subgroup U) (α β : U)
  (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
  (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
  let A := MonoidAlgebra Complex H
  let B := MonoidAlgebra Complex G
  let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ
  let φ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a)
  let ψ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b)
  let orbit := fun g : G =>
    Set.range (fun h : H =>
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a h * g * (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b h)⁻¹)
  let OrbitIndex := {s : Finset G // ∃ g : G, (s : Set G) = orbit g}
  let orbitSum := fun i : OrbitIndex =>
    Finset.sum (Subtype.val i) (fun g => MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : Complex))
  let HomSpace : Submodule Complex (LinearMap (RingHom.id Complex) B B) :=
    { carrier := { f |
        (∀ s x : B, f (s * x) = s * f x) ∧
        (∀ (r : A) (x : B), f (x * φ r) = f x * ψ r) }
      zero_mem' := by
        simp
      add_mem' := by
        rintro f g ⟨hfL, hfR⟩ ⟨hgL, hgR⟩
        exact ⟨fun s x => by simp [hfL, hgL, mul_add],
          fun r x => by simp [hfR, hgR, add_mul]⟩
      smul_mem' := by
        rintro c f ⟨hfL, hfR⟩
        exact ⟨fun s x => by simp [hfL],
          fun r x => by simp [hfR]⟩ }
  ∃ basis : Module.Basis OrbitIndex Complex HomSpace,
    (∀ (i : OrbitIndex) (x : B), Subtype.val (basis i) x = x * orbitSum i) ∧
    (∀ g : G, (∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b, MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element d = g) ↔ orbit g = {g}) ∧
    (Finite H → ∀ i : OrbitIndex,
      ∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up b),
        ∀ x : B,
          MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval d) (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) =
            MonoidAlgebra.coeff (Subtype.val (basis i) x))
```

## FiniteOrbitSumDiagram: Orbit-sum diagram from a reverse cup and multiplication cap

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

The space of bimodule maps from \(\I_{\bar\alpha}^{G,H}\) to
\(\I_{\bar\beta}^{G,H}\) has a basis given by right multiplication
by the sums of the finite orbits of
\[
       h\cdot g=\alpha_*(h)g\,\beta_*(h)^{-1}
       \qquad(h\in H,\ g\in G).
\]
The single group-element dots are the singleton orbits. If \(H\) is
finite, the sum over each orbit is realized by a diagram.

For finite \(H\), insert the reverse cup for \(1\hookrightarrow H\)
on the right of the \(\bar\alpha\)-strand. Merge the two induction
strands to an induction from \(1\) to \(G\), put the dot \(g\) on
that strand, then split using the \(\bar\beta\)-strand and apply the
multiplication cap for \(1\hookrightarrow H\). The resulting value
at \(x\) is
\[
 x\sum_{t\in H}\alpha_*(t^{-1})g\beta_*(t)
   =x\,|\operatorname{Stab}_H(g)|\sum_{z\in H\cdot g}z .
\]
The stabilizer order is invertible in \(\C\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 10](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, Proposition 3.3 and the finite orbit-sum diagram in its proof, p. 10. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash, and the task context supplies no statement correction or Alphabeta counterpart for this endpoint. The type retains the orbit-sum basis and singleton-dot criterion for arbitrary H. For finite H it expresses the right-hand reverse cup for the trivial subgroup, induction merge, group-element dot, induction split and multiplication cap as a typed composite with the required unitors and associators. It records the sum over H, the stabilizer-order multiple of the distinct orbit sum, the invertibility of that order over Complex, and the evaluation of the normalized diagram as the corresponding basis map. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem FiniteOrbitSumDiagram : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (H G : Subgroup U) (α β : U)
  (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
  (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
  let A := MonoidAlgebra Complex H
  let B := MonoidAlgebra Complex G
  let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ
  let φ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a)
  let ψ := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom Complex Complex (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b)
  let action := fun (h : H) (g : G) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a h * g * (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b h)⁻¹
  let orbit := fun g : G => Set.range (fun h : H => action h g)
  let OrbitIndex := {s : Finset G // ∃ g : G, (s : Set G) = orbit g}
  let orbitSum := fun i : OrbitIndex =>
    Finset.sum (Subtype.val i) (fun g => MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : Complex))
  let HomSpace : Submodule Complex (LinearMap (RingHom.id Complex) B B) :=
    { carrier := { f |
        (∀ s x : B, f (s * x) = s * f x) ∧
        (∀ (r : A) (x : B), f (x * φ r) = f x * ψ r) }
      zero_mem' := by
        simp
      add_mem' := by
        rintro f g ⟨hfL, hfR⟩ ⟨hgL, hgR⟩
        exact ⟨fun s x => by simp [hfL, hgL, mul_add],
          fun r x => by simp [hfR, hgR, add_mul]⟩
      smul_mem' := by
        rintro c f ⟨hfL, hfR⟩
        exact ⟨fun s x => by simp [hfL],
          fun r x => by simp [hfR]⟩ }
  ∃ basis : Module.Basis OrbitIndex Complex HomSpace,
    (∀ (i : OrbitIndex) (x : B), Subtype.val (basis i) x = x * orbitSum i) ∧
    (∀ g : G, (∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b, MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element d = g) ↔ orbit g = {g}) ∧
    (∀ [Finite H],
      let T : Subgroup U := ⊥
      let j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T H :=
        MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator (1 : U) (by
          intro t
          have ht : (t : U) = 1 := Subgroup.mem_bot.mp t.property
          simp [ht])
      let finiteIndex : Subgroup.FiniteIndex (MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom j)) :=
        Subgroup.finiteIndex_of_finite
      let p := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a
      let q := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up b
      let up := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up j
      let down := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down j
      let groupElements : Finset H := @Finset.univ H (Fintype.ofFinite H)
      ∀ g : G,
        let finiteOrbit : Set.Finite (orbit g) := Set.finite_range (fun h : H => action h g)
        let i : OrbitIndex :=
          ⟨Set.Finite.toFinset finiteOrbit, ⟨g, Set.Finite.coe_toFinset finiteOrbit⟩⟩
        let order : Complex := (Nat.card {h : H // action h g = g} : Complex)
        let dot : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp a j)
            (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp b j) :=
          { element := g
            intertwines := by
              intro t
              have ht : t = 1 := Subtype.ext (Subgroup.mem_bot.mp t.property)
              rw [ht, map_one, map_one, one_mul, mul_one] }
        let cup := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id p) (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.reverseCup (R := Complex) j finiteIndex)
        let merge := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.mergeUp (R := Complex) a j) (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id down)
        let dotStep := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.upDot (R := Complex) dot) (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id down)
        let split := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.splitUp (R := Complex) b j) (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id down)
        let cap := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id q) (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.multiplicationCap (R := Complex) j)
        let d : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex p q :=
          MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.insertRightUnit p)
            (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical cup
              (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate p up down)
                (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical merge
                  (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical dotStep
                    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical split
                      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate q up down)
                        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical cap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.rightUnit q))))))))
        let sumOverH : B := Finset.sum groupElements (fun t =>
          MonoidAlgebra.single
            (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a t⁻¹ * g * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b t)
            (1 : Complex))
        IsUnit order ∧
        (∀ x : B,
          MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval d)
              (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) = MonoidAlgebra.coeff (x * sumOverH) ∧
          x * sumOverH = x * (order • orbitSum i)) ∧
        (∀ x : B,
          MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap
              (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.scale order⁻¹ d))
              (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) = MonoidAlgebra.coeff (Subtype.val (basis i) x)))
```

## FiniteParabolicConjugateBlocks: Block formula for conjugation of a finite parabolic

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Let \(S_\infty\) be the group of finitely supported permutations of
\(\mathbb N\). A finite parabolic subgroup is a product
\(\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(X_i)\), where the \(X_i\) are pairwise
disjoint finite subsets of \(\mathbb N\) and \(I\) is finite. Each factor fixes the
complement of \(X_i\) pointwise. Omit empty blocks. The trivial group
is allowed. When comparing two such groups, take a finite set \(X\) containing both
unions of blocks and add singleton blocks so that both collections
partition \(X\).

If \(H=\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(X_i)\) and \(\alpha\in S_\infty\), then
\[
 \cg{\alpha}{H}=\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(\alpha(X_i)).
\]
Indeed, \((\alpha h\alpha^{-1})(\alpha(x))=\alpha(h(x))\) for \(x\in X_i\).
This preserves \(\alpha(X_i)\) for every \(h\in H\). Conversely, a
permutation preserving these images and fixing their complement
conjugates back to a permutation in \(H\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7, proof of Proposition 7.1, Conjugation, p. 28](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, § 7, Proposition 7.1, Conjugation, p. 28. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and the plan supplies no portal correction for this endpoint. Mathlib identifies the swap closure with the finitely supported permutations. The supremum of the disjoint embedded block factors represents their product. The empty index type gives the trivial group, and singleton padding contributes only trivial factors. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem FiniteParabolicConjugateBlocks : ∀ {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (X : ι → Finset Nat),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (X i)) →
  Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (X i) (X j)) →
  ∀ α : ↥(Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}),
    let blockProduct : (ι → Finset Nat) → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
      fun blocks => iSup (fun i =>
        MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ blocks i)))
    Subgroup.map
        (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj (α : Equiv.Perm Nat)))
        (blockProduct X) =
      blockProduct (fun i => Finset.image (α : Equiv.Perm Nat) (X i))
```

## FiniteParabolicIntersectionBlocks: Block formula for the intersection of two finite parabolics

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For \(A=\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(A_i)\) and
\(B=\prod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Sym}(B_j)\), use blocks that partition the same
finite set \(X\). A permutation of \(X\) preserves every \(A_i\) and
every \(B_j\) exactly when it preserves every \(A_i\cap B_j\).
Thus
\[
 A\cap B=\prod_{i\in I}\prod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Sym}(A_i\cap B_j),
\]
where empty intersections contribute trivial factors.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7, proof of Proposition 7.1, Intersection, pp. 28–29](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and the task context supplied no correction for this endpoint. Each block permutation is extended by the identity on its complement in Nat. The subgroup supremum represents the product of the disjoint block factors, with empty intersections contributing trivial subgroups. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
    (A : ι → Finset Nat) (B : κ → Finset Nat),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ i, n ∈ A i) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ j, n ∈ B j) →
  let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
    fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ S))
  (iSup (fun i => blockSym (A i))) ⊓ (iSup (fun j => blockSym (B j))) =
    iSup (fun i => iSup (fun j => blockSym (A i ∩ B j)))
```

## FiniteParabolicJoinBlocks: Connected-component block formula for the join of two finite parabolics

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For \(A=\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(A_i)\) and
\(B=\prod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Sym}(B_j)\), use blocks that partition the same
finite set \(X\). A permutation of \(X\) preserves every \(A_i\) and
every \(B_j\) exactly when it preserves every \(A_i\cap B_j\).
Thus
\[
 A\cap B=\prod_{i\in I}\prod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Sym}(A_i\cap B_j),
\]
where empty intersections contribute trivial factors.

Join \(A_i\) to \(B_j\) in a graph whenever \(A_i\cap B_j\ne\varnothing\).
For each connected component, let \(\widetilde{AB}^{(k)}\) be the
union of its blocks. Each point lies in an \(A\)-block and a \(B\)-block
joined by an edge, so either side gives the same union. The components give the
minimal nonempty collections of blocks on the two sides with a
common union, since any such collection contains every neighbor of
each selected block.

Both \(A\) and \(B\) preserve each \(\widetilde{AB}^{(k)}\). Inside \(\widetilde{AB}^{(k)}\), a path of
overlapping blocks joins any two points. Choosing a point in each
overlap gives a chain whose consecutive transpositions belong to
\(A\) or \(B\). After removing repetitions, successive applications of
\((x\,z)=(y\,z)(x\,y)(y\,z)\) give the transposition of the endpoints.
Since transpositions generate each symmetric group, the join is
\(\langle A\cup B\rangle=\prod_k\operatorname{Sym}(\widetilde{AB}^{(k)})\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7, proof of Proposition 7.1, Subgroup generated by a union, p. 29](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

The published PDF matches the project copy. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and the task context supplies no correction for this endpoint. The symmetric groups act by extension by the identity outside their blocks, so the join computed in Equiv.Perm Nat represents the join of the same finitely supported permutations in S∞. The supremum over the disjoint component blocks represents their product. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem FiniteParabolicJoinBlocks : ∀ {ι : Type*} {κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ] (X : Finset Nat)
    (A : ι → Finset Nat) (B : κ → Finset Nat),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ i, n ∈ A i) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ j, n ∈ B j) →
  let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
    fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ S))
  let block : Sum ι κ → Finset Nat := Sum.elim A B
  let graph : SimpleGraph (Sum ι κ) := SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v =>
    match u, v with
    | Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j => Finset.Nonempty (A i ∩ B j)
    | _, _ => False
  let componentBlock : SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent graph → Finset Nat := fun c =>
    let inComponent : Nat → Prop := fun n =>
      ∃ v : Sum ι κ, SimpleGraph.connectedComponentMk graph v = c ∧ n ∈ block v
    @Finset.filter Nat inComponent (Classical.decPred inComponent) X
  ((iSup fun i => blockSym (A i)) ⊔ (iSup fun j => blockSym (B j))) =
    iSup fun c => blockSym (componentBlock c)
```

## FiniteParabolicClosure: Closure of finite parabolics

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Let \(S_\infty\) be the group of finitely supported permutations of
\(\mathbb N\). A finite parabolic subgroup is a product
\(\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Sym}(X_i)\), where the \(X_i\) are pairwise
disjoint finite subsets of \(\mathbb N\) and \(I\) is finite. Each factor fixes the
complement of \(X_i\) pointwise. Omit empty blocks. The trivial group
is allowed. When comparing two such groups, take a finite set \(X\) containing both
unions of blocks and add singleton blocks so that both collections
partition \(X\).

Finite parabolic subgroups are closed under conjugation in
\(S_\infty\), pairwise intersections, and forming the subgroup
generated by two of them.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 7.1 [prop:parabolic-closure], p. 28](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7, Proposition 7.1 (Closure of finite parabolics, prop:parabolic-closure), printed p. 30 in the published PDF and p. 28 in the project PDF. Both copies give the same proposition. The configured defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, so any correction for Proposition 7.1 remains unverified. The swap closure represents finitely supported permutations, and the supremum represents the product of the disjoint block factors. The empty family gives the trivial subgroup. The binary clauses use the common finite carrier X obtained by singleton padding. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem FiniteParabolicClosure : (
  let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
    fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun m : Nat => m ∈ S))
  let parabolicOn : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) → Prop :=
    fun X H =>
      ∃ (n : Nat) (blocks : Fin n → Finset Nat),
        (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (blocks i)) ∧
        Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (blocks i) (blocks j)) ∧
        (∀ m : Nat, m ∈ X ↔ ∃ i, m ∈ blocks i) ∧
        H = iSup (fun i => blockSym (blocks i))
  let parabolic : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) → Prop :=
    fun H => ∃ X, parabolicOn X H
  (∀ (H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat)), parabolic H →
    ∀ α : ↥(Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}),
      parabolic (Subgroup.map
        (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj (α : Equiv.Perm Nat))) H)) ∧
  (∀ (X : Finset Nat) (H K : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat)),
    parabolicOn X H → parabolicOn X K →
      parabolicOn X (H ⊓ K) ∧ parabolicOn X (H ⊔ K))
)
```

## ExtremalParabolicsOfFiniteGroup: Parabolic subgroups below and above a finite group

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Let \(P\le S_\infty\) be finite. Its largest parabolic subgroup is
generated by all transpositions in \(P\). Its smallest parabolic
overgroup is the product of the symmetric groups on its
nonsingleton orbits.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Lemma 7.2 [lem:extremal-parabolics], p. 29](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Lemma 7.2 (lem:extremal-parabolics), printed p. 29 of the archived project PDF source/mackey-bimodules.pdf. The same statement appears on printed p. 31 of the current published PDF and on the author’s article page. The published PDF has a different SHA-256 digest from the archive and matches article-revision/mackey-bimodules.pdf. The configured defect report returned HTTP 404 both with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplies no correction for Lemma 7.2. The 27 November 2026 owner clarification concerns dot labels and geometric shape. The swap closure represents the finitely supported permutations. Each block symmetric group fixes its complement pointwise, and the supremum over the distinct nonsingleton orbit blocks represents their product. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams#lem:extremal-parabolics https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ExtremalParabolicsOfFiniteGroup : (
  let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
    fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun m : Nat => m ∈ S))
  let parabolicOn : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) → Prop :=
    fun X H =>
      ∃ (n : Nat) (blocks : Fin n → Finset Nat),
        (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (blocks i)) ∧
        Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (blocks i) (blocks j)) ∧
        (∀ m : Nat, m ∈ X ↔ ∃ i, m ∈ blocks i) ∧
        H = iSup (fun i => blockSym (blocks i))
  let parabolic : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) → Prop :=
    fun H => ∃ X, parabolicOn X H
  ∀ (P : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat)) [Finite ↥P],
    P ≤ Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ} →
    let lower := Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | σ ∈ P ∧ Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}
    let orbitBlocks : Set (Finset Nat) :=
      {S | (∃ x : Nat, (↑S : Set Nat) = MulAction.orbit ↥P x) ∧
        Set.Nontrivial (↑S : Set Nat)}
    let upper := iSup (fun S : ↥orbitBlocks => blockSym (Subtype.val S))
    IsGreatest {H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) | parabolic H ∧ H ≤ P} lower ∧
      IsLeast {H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) | parabolic H ∧ P ≤ H} upper
)
```

## BlockwiseGroupElementDotCriterion: Blockwise criterion for group-element dots

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Suppose \(H,G\) are products of symmetric groups on disjoint
blocks in the group of finitely supported permutations. Each
embedding sends a non-singleton \(H\)-block into a \(G\)-block.
A dot exists exactly when the two images of each non-singleton
\(H\)-block lie in the same \(G\)-block. Necessity follows by
testing transpositions. For sufficiency extend
\(\beta(x)\mapsto\alpha(x)\) on those images to permutations in
the \(G\)-blocks. These partial bijections differ from the
identity at finitely many points, so the extensions can have
finite support. Together they give a dot in \(G\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, A criterion for group-element dots, p. 11](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.4, “A criterion for group-element dots,” p. 11. The published PDF matched the project copy byte for byte, and the project TeX and article HTML agree on the endpoint. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplies no corrected statement. The swap closure models the finitary symmetric group on Nat. Each block factor fixes its complement pointwise, and the subgroup supremum represents the product of the disjoint factors inside that finitary group. The block families and blocks may be infinite. The type includes the containment assertion for both embeddings and uses MackeyDiagrams.Dot for existence of a group-element dot. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem BlockwiseGroupElementDotCriterion : ∀ {ι κ : Type*} (X : ι → Set Nat) (Y : κ → Set Nat),
  (∀ i, Set.Nonempty (X i)) → (∀ j, Set.Nonempty (Y j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (X i) (X i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (Y j) (Y j')) →
  let U := Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}
  let blockSym := fun B : Set Nat => _root_.fixingSubgroup (↥U) Bᶜ
  let H := iSup (fun i => blockSym (X i))
  let G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (Y j))
  ∀ (α β : ↥U)
      (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : ↥U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
      (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : ↥U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
    let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
    let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ
    let inBlock := fun (σ : ↥U) (i : ι) (j : κ) =>
      Set.MapsTo (⇑(σ : Equiv.Perm Nat)) (X i) (Y j)
    (∀ i, Set.Nontrivial (X i) →
      (∃ j, inBlock α i j) ∧ (∃ j, inBlock β i j)) ∧
    (Nonempty (MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b) ↔
      ∀ i, Set.Nontrivial (X i) → ∃ j, inBlock α i j ∧ inBlock β i j)
```

## BlockSwapOrbitSumWithoutGroupDot: A block swap

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Let
\[
 B_1=\{1,2,3\},\quad B_2=\{4,5,6\},\quad
 B_3=\{7,8,9\},\quad B_4=\{10,11,12\}.
\]
Put
\[
 G=\operatorname{Sym}(B_1\cup B_2)\times\operatorname{Sym}(B_3\cup B_4),
 \qquad H=\prod_{i=1}^4\operatorname{Sym}(B_i).
\]
Take \(\alpha=(4\,7)(5\,8)(6\,9)\) and \(\beta=1\).
The embeddings send \((4\,5)\) to transpositions in different
\(G\)-blocks. Every element of \(G\) preserves the two blocks,
so there is no group-element dot between these embeddings.
The sum over the orbit of \(1\) gives a nonzero diagram map by
Proposition~3.3.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.3 [ex:block-swap], p. 10](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.3 [ex:block-swap], p. 10. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the project TeX and article HTML agree on the example. The defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplies no statement correction or Alphabeta counterpart for this example. The ambient swap closure represents the finitary symmetric group on Nat. Each block factor fixes its complement pointwise, and each subgroup supremum represents the product of the disjoint factors. The type records the two conjugation embeddings, the images of (4 5), block preservation by G, the absence of a group-element dot, and a typed induction diagram whose nonzero evaluation is right multiplication by the distinct orbit sum of the identity over Complex. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem BlockSwapOrbitSumWithoutGroupDot : let B₁ : Set Nat := {1, 2, 3}
  let B₂ : Set Nat := {4, 5, 6}
  let B₃ : Set Nat := {7, 8, 9}
  let B₄ : Set Nat := {10, 11, 12}
  let X : Fin 4 → Set Nat := ![B₁, B₂, B₃, B₄]
  let Y : Fin 2 → Set Nat := ![B₁ ∪ B₂, B₃ ∪ B₄]
  let U := Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}
  let blockSym := fun B : Set Nat => _root_.fixingSubgroup (↥U) Bᶜ
  let H := iSup (fun i => blockSym (X i))
  let G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (Y j))
  let swap := fun (i j : Nat) (hij : i ≠ j) =>
    (⟨Equiv.swap i j, Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨i, j, hij, rfl⟩⟩ : ↥U)
  let α := swap 4 7 (by decide) * swap 5 8 (by decide) * swap 6 9 (by decide)
  let β : ↥U := 1
  ∃ (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : ↥U) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
    (hβ : ∀ h : H, β * (h : ↥U) * β⁻¹ ∈ G),
    let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
    let b := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ
    let orbit := Set.range (fun h : H =>
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a h * (1 : G) *
        (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b h)⁻¹)
    (∀ (g : G) (j : Fin 2), Set.MapsTo (⇑((g : ↥U) : Equiv.Perm Nat)) (Y j) (Y j)) ∧
    (∃ t : H,
      ((t : ↥U) : Equiv.Perm Nat) = Equiv.swap 4 5 ∧
      (((MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a t : G) : ↥U) : Equiv.Perm Nat) =
        Equiv.swap 7 8 ∧
      (((MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b t : G) : ↥U) : Equiv.Perm Nat) =
        Equiv.swap 4 5) ∧
    ¬ Nonempty (MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b) ∧
    ∃ s : Finset G, (s : Set G) = orbit ∧
      let B := MonoidAlgebra Complex G
      let orbitSum : B := Finset.sum s (fun g => MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : Complex))
      ∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up b),
        let f := MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval d)
        f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x : B, f (MonoidAlgebra.coeff x) = MonoidAlgebra.coeff (x * orbitSum)
```

```lean
theorem DotBetweenImagesInOneBlock : let U := Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)
let B : Finset (Fin 4) := {0, 1}
let H : Subgroup U := iInf (fun x : {x : Fin 4 // x ∉ B} => MulAction.stabilizer U x.val)
let G : Subgroup U := ⊤
let α : U := 1
let β : U := Equiv.swap (1 : Fin 4) 2
let a : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α (fun _ => Subgroup.mem_top _)
let b : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G :=
  MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β (fun _ => Subgroup.mem_top _)
Finset.image (fun x => α x) B ≠ Finset.image (fun x => β x) B ∧
  ∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Dot a b, (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element d : U) = β
```

## StrongerEmbeddingConditionSlideObstruction: A reverse slide under the stronger embedding condition

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Fix a representative \(\beta\) for the embedding of \(K\) into \(H\).
Suppose \(\cg{\sigma\beta^{-1}}{H}\le G\) whenever
\(\cg{\sigma}{K}\le G\). A reverse slide onto the right leg
can still fail.

Use
\(K=\prod_i\operatorname{Sym}(B_i)\),
\(H=\operatorname{Sym}(B_1\cup B_2)\times\operatorname{Sym}(B_3\cup B_4)\),
\(G=S_{\{1,\ldots,12\}}\), and \(\beta=1\). If
\(\cg{\sigma}{K}\le G\), the support of \(\cg{\sigma}{K}\) forces
\(\sigma\) to preserve \(\{1,\ldots,12\}\), so
\(\cg{\sigma}{H}\le G\). The block swap \(\alpha=(4\,7)(5\,8)(6\,9)\)
conjugates \(K\) to itself and lies in \(G\setminus H\).
It labels a dot on the merged strand from the inclusion to
\(\bar\alpha\). It cannot move to the right input because it lies
outside \(H\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.5 [ex:stronger-slide-obstruction], p. 11](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

### Lean statement

Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.5 [ex:stronger-slide-obstruction], p. 11, including the preceding stronger embedding condition. The block definitions are those of Example 3.3, and the induction-merge drawing on p. 9 specifies the two marked positions. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the author’s HTML reproduces Example 3.5. The swap closure models the finitary symmetric group on Nat, and each symmetric block factor fixes its complement pointwise. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams#ex:stronger-slide-obstruction

The 27 November 2026 owner clarification (translation recheck request f13b4bd8ba9fe139) governs both marked vertices. The merged mark is the coefficient-one singleton at α. The obstruction excludes every finite complex label of termwise eligible group elements on the right leg, comparing the evaluations of the two trivalent drawings at the fixed boundary with inclusion inputs and output embedding represented by α.

The designated defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplied no correction for Example 3.5. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem StrongerEmbeddingConditionSlideObstruction : let Sfin : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  Subgroup.closure {σ : Equiv.Perm Nat | Equiv.Perm.IsSwap σ}
let U := ↥Sfin
let B : Fin 4 → Set Nat := fun i =>
  Set.Icc (3 * (i : Nat) + 1) (3 * (i : Nat) + 3)
let blockSym : Set Nat → Subgroup U := fun X => _root_.fixingSubgroup U Xᶜ
let K : Subgroup U := iSup (fun i => blockSym (B i))
let H : Subgroup U :=
  blockSym (B 0 ∪ B 1) ⊔ blockSym (B 2 ∪ B 3)
let G : Subgroup U := blockSym (Set.Icc 1 12)
let β : U := 1
let swapInU : (i j : Nat) → i ≠ j → U := fun i j hij =>
  ⟨Equiv.swap i j, Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨i, j, hij, rfl⟩⟩
let α : U :=
  swapInU 4 7 (by decide) * swapInU 5 8 (by decide) * swapInU 6 9 (by decide)
let conj : U → Subgroup U → Subgroup U := fun σ L =>
  Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj σ)) L
(∀ σ : U, conj σ K ≤ G → conj (σ * β⁻¹) H ≤ G) ∧
  conj α K = K ∧ α ∉ H ∧
  ∃ (hKH : K ≤ H) (hHG : H ≤ G) (hα : α ∈ G),
    let ιKH : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H :=
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β (fun k => by
        change (1 : U) * (k : U) * (1 : U)⁻¹ ∈ H
        simpa only [one_mul, inv_one, mul_one] using hKH k.property)
    let ιHG : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G :=
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator 1 (fun h => by
        simpa only [one_mul, inv_one, mul_one] using hHG h.property)
    let incl := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp ιHG ιKH
    let target : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K G :=
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α (fun k =>
        G.mul_mem (G.mul_mem hα (hHG (hKH k.property))) (G.inv_mem hα))
    let input := MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up ιHG) (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up ιKH)
    ∃ d : MackeyDiagrams.Dot incl target,
      MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element d = (⟨α, hα⟩ : G) ∧
      let onMerged : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex input (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up target) :=
        MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent
            (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp ιHG ιKH))
          (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing
            (Finsupp.single d (1 : Complex) : MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex incl target))
      ¬ ∃ (b : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H)
          (label : MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex ιKH b)
          (h : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp ιHG b = target),
        let onRight : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex input
            (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp ιHG b)) :=
          MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
                (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up ιHG)))
              (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.upDrawing label))
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.trivalent
              (MackeyDiagrams.TrivalentVertex.mergeUp ιHG b))
        MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret
              (Eq.ndrec (motive := fun out =>
                MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex input (MackeyDiagrams.Word.up out))
                onRight h)) =
          MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret onMerged)
```

## SupportBoundsUnderComposition: Support bounds under composition

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For a finite subgroup \(X\) given by symmetric groups on disjoint
blocks, let \(\operatorname{supp}X\) be the union of its non-singleton blocks
and \(\widehat X=\operatorname{Sym}(\operatorname{supp}X)\). The conditions
\(\alpha\in G\widehat H\) and \(\beta\in H\widehat K\) do not ensure
\(\alpha\beta\in G\widehat K\).

Take
\[
 G=H=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,6\})
         \times\operatorname{Sym}(\{7,\ldots,12\}),
 \qquad K=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3\}).
\]
Let \(\alpha\) swap the two six-point blocks and let \(\beta=1\).
The two embeddings satisfy the support bounds.
Every element of \(G\widehat K\) preserves each six-point block,
whereas \(\alpha\beta\) carries the support of \(K\) into the second
block. Even the composite strand label has no representative
in \(G\widehat K\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.6 [ex:support-composite], p. 11](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.6 (ex:support-composite), p. 11. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the article webpage reproduces the example. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404. The task context supplies no corrected endpoint. Each block symmetric group acts by extension by the identity in Equiv.Perm Nat. The subgroup supremum represents the direct product of the disjoint block factors, and the support bounds use pointwise set products. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem SupportBoundsUnderComposition : let A : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 6
let B : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 7 12
let supportK : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 3
let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ S))
let subgroupProduct : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) →
    Set (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  fun S T => Set.image2 (fun x y => x * y) (S : Set (Equiv.Perm Nat))
    (T : Set (Equiv.Perm Nat))
let G := blockSym A ⊔ blockSym B
let H := G
let K := blockSym supportK
let Hhat := blockSym (A ∪ B)
let Khat := blockSym supportK
let β : Equiv.Perm Nat := 1
∃ (α : Equiv.Perm Nat)
    (hα : ∀ h : H, α * (h : Equiv.Perm Nat) * α⁻¹ ∈ G)
    (hβ : ∀ k : K, β * (k : Equiv.Perm Nat) * β⁻¹ ∈ H),
  Finset.image α A = B ∧
  Finset.image α B = A ∧
  α ∈ subgroupProduct G Hhat ∧
  β ∈ subgroupProduct H Khat ∧
  (∀ γ ∈ subgroupProduct G Khat, Finset.image γ A = A ∧ Finset.image γ B = B) ∧
  Set.MapsTo (⇑(α * β)) (supportK : Set Nat) (B : Set Nat) ∧
  α * β ∉ subgroupProduct G Khat ∧
  ¬ ∃ (γ : Equiv.Perm Nat) (_ : γ ∈ subgroupProduct G Khat)
      (hγ : ∀ k : K, γ * (k : Equiv.Perm Nat) * γ⁻¹ ∈ G),
    MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator γ hγ =
      MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp
        (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα)
        (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator β hβ)
```

## SupportBoundsForInverseProduct: Support bounds for an inverse product

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Consider whether \(\cg{\beta\alpha^{-1}}{H}\le G\)
when \(\alpha,\beta\in\widehat G H\) both embed \(H\) in \(G\). Take \(G\) to be the product of the symmetric groups on
\(\{1,2\},\{3,4\},\{5,6\}\), \(H=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2\})\),
\(\alpha=(1\,3)(2\,4)\), and \(\beta=(4\,5)\).
Both permutations belong to \(\widehat G H\) and embed \(H\) in \(G\).
But \(\beta\alpha^{-1}\) sends \(\{1,2\}\) to \(\{3,5\}\), so
\(\cg{\beta\alpha^{-1}}{H}\nleq G\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.7 [ex:support-inverse-product], p. 11](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 3.7 (ex:support-inverse-product), p. 11. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the article webpage reproduces the example. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404. The task context supplies no corrected endpoint. The block symmetric groups are extended by the identity in Equiv.Perm Nat, so their actions are finitary. The supremum of the three disjoint block groups represents their direct product, and the support bound uses the pointwise set product in the order Ghat H. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem SupportBoundsForInverseProduct : let A : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 2
let B : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 3 4
let C : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 5 6
let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ S))
let G := blockSym A ⊔ blockSym B ⊔ blockSym C
let H := blockSym A
let Ghat := blockSym (A ∪ B ∪ C)
let bound : Set (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  Set.image2 (fun x y => x * y) (Ghat : Set (Equiv.Perm Nat)) (H : Set (Equiv.Perm Nat))
let conjugate : Equiv.Perm Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  fun σ S => Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj σ)) S
let α : Equiv.Perm Nat := Equiv.swap 1 3 * Equiv.swap 2 4
let β : Equiv.Perm Nat := Equiv.swap 4 5
let γ := β * α⁻¹
α ∈ bound ∧
  β ∈ bound ∧
  conjugate α H ≤ G ∧
  conjugate β H ≤ G ∧
  Finset.image γ A = ({3, 5} : Finset Nat) ∧
  ¬ (conjugate γ H ≤ G)
```

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.5, Proposition 3.4, multiplication-cap row, p. 12. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The typed diagrams follow the original TikZ, with bottom strands labelled by γα and α and the top strand by γ. The equality is over the complex group algebras at arbitrary index. The Lean type elaborated through the shared compilation slot. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404. The task context supplies no corrected statement for this endpoint. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem MultiplicationCapBend : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (K H G : Subgroup U) (α γ : U)
    (hα : ∀ k : K, α * (k : U) * α⁻¹ ∈ H)
    (hγ : ∀ h : H, γ * (h : U) * γ⁻¹ ∈ G),
  let a := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator α hα
  let g := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.ofConjugator γ hγ
  let ga := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp g a
  let upG := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up g
  let upA := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up a
  let upGA := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up ga
  let downA := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down a
  let downG := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down g
  let downGA := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down ga
  let straight := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) upG
  let leftCap := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal straight
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.multiplicationCap a)
  let leftSplit := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.splitUp g a) (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id downA)
  let left := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical leftSplit
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate upG upA downA)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical leftCap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.rightUnit upG)))
  let rightCup := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id downA)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.ordinaryCup (R := Complex) g)
  let rightBranch := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.insertRightUnit downA)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical rightCup
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate downA downG upG)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.mergeDown g a) straight)))
  let rightCap := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.multiplicationCap ga) straight
  let right := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upGA) rightBranch)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate upGA downGA upG)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical rightCap (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.leftUnit upG)))
  MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval left = MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval right
```

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 3.5, Proposition 3.4, Trace-cap bend, p. 12. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The source TikZ fixes the bottom word at K–G–H and the top word at K–H. The two diagrams have this same boundary over the complex group algebras. The finite-index hypothesis applies to the image of α in H. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No correction for this endpoint was available. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem TraceCapBend : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (K H G : Subgroup U)
    (α : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H) (γ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G)
    (finite : Subgroup.FiniteIndex (MonoidHom.range (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom α))),
  let composite := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp γ α
  let downComposite := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down composite
  let upComposite := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up composite
  let downGamma := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down γ
  let upGamma := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up γ
  let upAlpha := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up α
  let output := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down α
  let input := MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor downComposite upGamma
  let idOutput := MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) output
  let left : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex input output :=
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.splitDown γ α)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upGamma))
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate output downGamma upGamma)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal idOutput (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.traceCap γ))
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.rightUnit output)))
  let rightBranch : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex upGamma
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor upComposite output) :=
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.insertRightUnit upGamma)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upGamma)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.reverseCup α finite))
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate upGamma upAlpha output)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.mergeUp γ α) idOutput)))
  let right : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex input output :=
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id downComposite) rightBranch)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate downComposite upComposite output)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.traceCap composite) idOutput)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.leftUnit output)))
  MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval left = MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval right
```

```lean
theorem OrdinaryCupBend : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (K H G : Subgroup U)
    (α : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding K H) (γ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H G),
  let composite := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp γ α
  let upAlpha := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up α
  let downAlpha := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down α
  let upGamma := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up γ
  let downGamma := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down γ
  let upComposite := MackeyDiagrams.Word.up composite
  let downComposite := MackeyDiagrams.Word.down composite
  let output := MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor downGamma upComposite
  let left : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex upAlpha output :=
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.insertLeftUnit upAlpha)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.ordinaryCup γ)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upAlpha))
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate downGamma upGamma upAlpha)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id downGamma)
            (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.mergeUp γ α))))
  let rightBranch : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor upAlpha downComposite) downGamma :=
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upAlpha)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.splitDown γ α))
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate upAlpha downAlpha downGamma)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.multiplicationCap α)
            (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id downGamma))
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.leftUnit downGamma)))
  let right : MackeyDiagrams.Diagram Complex upAlpha output :=
    MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.insertRightUnit upAlpha)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upAlpha)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.ordinaryCup composite))
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate upAlpha downComposite upComposite)
          (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.horizontal rightBranch
            (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id upComposite))))
  MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval left = MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.eval right
```

## ReverseCupBend: Reverse-cup bend
