```lean
theorem RightOrbitDiagramFromProjectedStabilizer : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (G A D F C E : Subgroup U)
    (a : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A G) (b : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A D)
    (d : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding F D) (c : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding C G)
    (e : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding C E) (f : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding F E),
  let up := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.up U _
  let down := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.down U _
  let tensor := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor U _
  let comp := @MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp U _
  let ga := up a
  let ad := down b
  let df := up d
  let gc := up c
  let ce := down e
  let ef := up f
  let bottom := tensor ga (tensor ad df)
  let top := tensor gc (tensor ce ef)
  let X := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis bottom
  let Y := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis top
  let Pair := X.carrier × Y.carrier
  let input := fun (g : G) (x : D) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction a)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ad df)) g (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair b d x)
  let output := fun (g : G) (y : E) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction c)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ce ef)) g (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair e f y)
  letI : MulAction (G × F) Pair :=
    { smul := fun q z => (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.act X q z.1, MackeyDiagrams.Biset.act Y q z.2)
      one_smul := fun z => Prod.ext (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.one_act X z.1)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.one_act Y z.2)
      mul_smul := fun q q' z => Prod.ext (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.mul_act X q q' z.1)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.mul_act Y q q' z.2) }
  let orbit : Pair → Set Pair := MulAction.orbit (G × F)
  let stabilizer : Pair → Subgroup (G × F) := MulAction.stabilizer (G × F)
  let projected := fun z : Pair =>
    Subgroup.map (MonoidHom.comp (Subgroup.subtype F) (MonoidHom.snd G F)) (stabilizer z)
  let coefficient := fun (M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y) (z : Pair) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap M (Finsupp.single z.1 (1 : Complex)) z.2
  let LowerLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp b i) (comp d j)
  let MiddleLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp c k)
  let UpperLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp e k) (comp f j)
  let Fiber := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) =>
    (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor (up i) (down j))).carrier
  let lowerMap := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (r : LowerLabel P i j) (w : Fiber P i j) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedMultiplicationBasis b d i j r w
  let finiteFibers := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (r : LowerLabel P i j) =>
    ∀ z : (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ad df)).carrier,
      Set.Finite {w | lowerMap P i j r w = z}
  let ProjectionTerm := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed b d i j
  let projectionTerm := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (r : LowerLabel P i j) (finite : finiteFibers P i j r) =>
    (⟨r, finite⟩ : ProjectionTerm P i j)
  let drawId := fun {K H : Subgroup U} (p : MackeyDiagrams.Word K H) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) p)
  let rightDrawing := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (lower : List (Complex × ProjectionTerm P i j))
      (middle : List (Complex × MiddleLabel P i k))
      (upper : List (Complex × UpperLabel P j k)) =>
    let ai := up i
    let fj := down j
    let ck := up k
    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId ga)
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection b d i j lower))
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ga ai fj))
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp a i c k middle) (drawId fj))
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate gc ck fj))
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId gc)
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication e f k j upper))))) :
      MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
  let singletonDrawing := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (r : LowerLabel P i j) (t : MiddleLabel P i k) (s : UpperLabel P j k)
      (finite : finiteFibers P i j r) =>
    rightDrawing P i j k [(1, projectionTerm P i j r finite)] [(1, t)] [(1, s)]
  let eval := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret drawing)
  let IsRightTerm := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
    ∃ (P : Subgroup U) (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (lower : List (Complex × ProjectionTerm P i j))
      (middle : List (Complex × MiddleLabel P i k))
      (upper : List (Complex × UpperLabel P j k)),
      drawing = rightDrawing P i j k lower middle upper
  (∀ (M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y) (z z' : Pair),
    z' ∈ orbit z → coefficient M z' = coefficient M z) ∧
  (∀ z : Pair, ∃ (r : D) (t : G) (s : E), z ∈ orbit (input 1 r, output t s)) ∧
  (∀ (r : D) (t : G) (s : E),
    let z₀ : Pair := (input 1 r, output t s)
    let P := projected z₀
    let O := orbit z₀
    (∀ h : F, (h : U) ∈ P ↔
      ∃ (α : A) (κ : C),
        r * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom d h * r⁻¹ =
          MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b α ∧
        s * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom f h * s⁻¹ =
          MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom e κ ∧
        MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a α =
          t * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom c κ * t⁻¹) ∧
    O = Set.range (fun q : G × F =>
      (input q.1 (r * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom d q.2),
       output (q.1 * t) (s * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom f q.2))) ∧
    (∀ (g g' : G) (x : D) (h : F),
      input g' (r * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom d h) = input g x ↔
        ∃ α : A, g' = g * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a α ∧
          x = MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom b α * r * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom d h) ∧
    ∃ (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
        (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
        (rDot : LowerLabel P i j) (tDot : MiddleLabel P i k) (sDot : UpperLabel P j k),
      (∀ h : P, (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom j h : U) = (h : U)) ∧
      MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element rDot = r ∧ MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element tDot = t ∧
      MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element sDot = s ∧
      (∀ q : G × F, q ∈ stabilizer z₀ ↔ ∃ h : P,
        q = (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom i h),
             MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom j h)) ∧
      (∀ (g : G) (x : D),
        Set.BijOn
          (fun w : Fiber P i j =>
            let v : A × F := Quotient.out w
            output (g * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom a v.1 * t)
              (s * MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom f v.2))
          {w | lowerMap P i j rDot w = MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair b d x}
          {y | (input g x, y) ∈ O}) ∧
      (∀ M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y, coefficient M z₀ ≠ 0 →
        (∀ p : X.carrier, Set.Finite {y | (p, y) ∈ O}) ∧
        ∃ finite : finiteFibers P i j rDot,
          ∀ z : Pair,
            coefficient (eval (singletonDrawing P i j k rDot tDot sDot finite)) z =
              @ite Complex (z ∈ O) (Classical.propDecidable (z ∈ O)) 1 0)) ∧
  (∀ (P : Subgroup U) (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (r : LowerLabel P i j) (t : MiddleLabel P i k) (s : UpperLabel P j k)
      (finite : finiteFibers P i j r) (z : Pair),
    coefficient (eval (singletonDrawing P i j k r t s finite)) z ≠ 0 →
      z ∈ orbit (input 1 (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element r),
        output (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t) (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element s))) ∧
  (∀ terms : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top),
    (∀ term ∈ terms, IsRightTerm term.2) →
    let drawing := List.foldr
      (fun term rest => MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.add
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale term.1 term.2) rest)
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
        (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.zero (R := Complex) bottom top)) terms
    Set.Finite {O : Set Pair | ∃ z : Pair,
      O = orbit z ∧ coefficient (eval drawing) z ≠ 0}) ∧
  (∀ (M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y) (p : X.carrier),
    Set.Finite {O : Set Pair | ∃ y : Y.carrier, coefficient M (p, y) ≠ 0 ∧ O = orbit (p, y)})
```

## ExpansionIntoRightDiagrams: Expansion into right diagrams

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

In each pair below, the left shape is \(s_1s_2s_1\) and the right shape is
\(s_2s_1s_2\). The numbers identify the direction of replacement.
Fix the boundary groups and the boundary strand cosets in each pair.
Letters such as \(a\) denote conjugation embeddings, and \(\bar a\) is
the coset of a representative of \(a\). Write \(ad=a\circ d\).
Write \(\operatorname{Ad}_p\) for conjugation by \(p\).

A label \(s\) on a mixed crossing denotes the parameter in
\(q_s([k,h])=\alpha(k)s\beta(h)\). The multiplication crossing is
\(q_s\). The projection uses the trace dot \(s^{-1}\) and sends
\[
 z\longmapsto q_s^!(z)=\sum_{q_s([k,h])=z}[k,h].
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-mixed-composition}, this formula applies
when the fibers of \(q_s\) are finite, even if the cup by itself
would have infinite index. In a composite with linear labels,
each projection must have finite fibers for every term used.

Write \(a:A\to G\), \(b:A\to D\), and \(d:F\to D\) for the lower
embeddings and \(c:C\to G\), \(e:C\to E\), and \(f:F\to E\) for the upper ones.
The source basis is \(G\times_A D\) and the target basis is \(G\times_C E\).

With this boundary, every bimodule map is a sum of right diagrams
under the finite-fiber convention, with only finitely many nonzero
terms on each input. A finite sum suffices exactly when only
finitely many \(G\times F\)-orbits of input--output basis pairs
have nonzero matrix coefficient. The group acts simultaneously
on the input and output.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Theorem 6.7 [thm:three-orbits], p. 26 (related source excerpts on pp. 22, 25–26)](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 6.3.1, Theorem 6.7 [thm:three-orbits], printed p. 26 of the archived project PDF source/mackey-bimodules.pdf. The archive gives the mixed-crossing convention on p. 22 and the fixed boundary and right shape on p. 25. The corresponding printed pages in the current published PDF are 28, 24 and 27, respectively. The current download has SHA-256 813c82da512e992a11a53aa044c3a79d199b2bef5295639084c1f6b789d27e61. Its convention on printed p. 6 specifies equality of evaluated bimodule maps at a common boundary, including pointwise-finite indexed sums. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

For each bimodule map at the fixed boundary, the pointwise sum has an existential index type, arbitrary complex weights on typed right diagrams, finite support on each input, and evaluation equal to the map. The independent finite-sum criterion compares evaluated finite combinations, including the empty combination, with finiteness of the supported simultaneous G × F orbits. The specific displayed identity for a left diagram on archived p. 27 and published p. 29 is the separate CaseFivePointwiseFiniteDiagramIdentity endpoint.

The 27 November 2026 owner clarification recorded in translation recheck request f13b4bd8ba9fe139 gives each of the three marks an independent finite complex linear label of termwise eligible group elements, including zero. The lower mixed projection requires finite fibers for each term’s multiplication parameter, the inverse of its trace dot. The middle mark is a parallel induction crossing and the upper mark is a mixed multiplication.

The designated article defect report returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. A statement correction for Theorem 6.7 could not be verified. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ExpansionIntoRightDiagrams : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (G A D F C E : Subgroup U)
    (a : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A G) (b : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A D)
    (d : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding F D) (c : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding C G)
    (e : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding C E) (f : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding F E),
  let up := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.up U _
  let down := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.down U _
  let tensor := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor U _
  let comp := @MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp U _
  let ga := up a
  let ad := down b
  let df := up d
  let gc := up c
  let ce := down e
  let ef := up f
  let bottom := tensor ga (tensor ad df)
  let top := tensor gc (tensor ce ef)
  let X := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis bottom
  let Y := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis top
  let Pair := X.carrier × Y.carrier
  letI : MulAction (G × F) Pair :=
    { smul := fun q z => (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.act X q z.1, MackeyDiagrams.Biset.act Y q z.2)
      one_smul := fun z => Prod.ext (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.one_act X z.1)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.one_act Y z.2)
      mul_smul := fun q q' z => Prod.ext (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.mul_act X q q' z.1)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.mul_act Y q q' z.2) }
  let orbit : Pair → Set Pair := MulAction.orbit (G × F)
  let coefficient := fun (M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y) (z : Pair) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap M (Finsupp.single z.1 (1 : Complex)) z.2
  let MiddleLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp c k)
  let UpperLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp e k) (comp f j)
  let ProjectionTerm := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed b d i j
  let drawId := fun {K H : Subgroup U} (p : MackeyDiagrams.Word K H) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) p)
  let rightDrawing := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (lower : List (Complex × ProjectionTerm P i j))
      (middle : List (Complex × MiddleLabel P i k))
      (upper : List (Complex × UpperLabel P j k)) =>
    let ai := up i
    let fj := down j
    let ck := up k
    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId ga)
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection b d i j lower))
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ga ai fj))
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp a i c k middle) (drawId fj))
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate gc ck fj))
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId gc)
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication e f k j upper))))) :
      MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
  let eval := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret drawing)
  let IsRightTerm := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
    ∃ (P : Subgroup U) (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (lower : List (Complex × ProjectionTerm P i j))
      (middle : List (Complex × MiddleLabel P i k))
      (upper : List (Complex × UpperLabel P j k)),
      drawing = rightDrawing P i j k lower middle upper
  ∀ (M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y),
    let supported : Set (Set Pair) := {O | ∃ z : Pair, O = orbit z ∧ coefficient M z ≠ 0}
    (∃ (I : type_of% U) (weight : I → Complex)
        (diagram : I → MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top),
      (∀ i, IsRightTerm (diagram i)) ∧
      let summand := fun i => MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (weight i) (diagram i)
      ∃ finite : ∀ v : Finsupp X.carrier Complex,
          Set.Finite (Function.support fun i =>
            MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (eval (summand i)) v),
        let expansion : MackeyDiagrams.PointwiseIndexedDrawing Complex bottom top I :=
          ⟨summand, finite⟩
        M = MackeyDiagrams.PointwiseIndexedDrawing.evalHom expansion) ∧
    ((∃ terms : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top),
        (∀ term ∈ terms, IsRightTerm term.2) ∧
        let expansion : MackeyDiagrams.IndexedDrawing Complex bottom top (Fin terms.length) :=
          ⟨Finset.univ, fun i =>
            MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (terms.get i).1 (terms.get i).2⟩
        MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap M = MackeyDiagrams.IndexedDrawing.eval expansion) ↔
      Set.Finite supported)
```

## CaseFivePointwiseFiniteDiagramIdentity: Case 5 pointwise finite orbit expansion of a left diagram

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Write \(a:A\to G\), \(b:A\to D\), and \(d:F\to D\) for the lower
embeddings and \(c:C\to G\), \(e:C\to E\), and \(f:F\to E\) for the upper ones.
The source basis is \(G\times_A D\) and the target basis is \(G\times_C E\).

With this boundary, every bimodule map is a sum of right diagrams
under the finite-fiber convention, with only finitely many nonzero
terms on each input. A finite sum suffices exactly when only
finitely many \(G\times F\)-orbits of input--output basis pairs
have nonzero matrix coefficient. The group acts simultaneously
on the input and output.

In the diagram, \(\mathcal S\) is the set of supported orbits,
\(P_{\mathcal O}\) is the projected pair stabilizer, and
\(c_{\mathcal O}\) is the matrix coefficient on the orbit.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. The endpoint is the displayed Case 5 identity immediately after Theorem 6.7 in § 6.3.1 of Ian Xiao’s Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, on printed p. 27 of the archived project PDF source/mackey-bimodules.pdf (SHA-256 bc57d13777e7df145b6dfd84029e0e9539fedb33d22b2823e14c096e4c3c12f2). The archive gives the fixed boundary and Theorem 6.7 on pp. 25–26 and the mixed-crossing convention on p. 22. The archived drawing and its TikZ give the two ordered crossing sequences.

The live PDF retrieved separately (SHA-256 813c82da512e992a11a53aa044c3a79d199b2bef5295639084c1f6b789d27e61) places the same displayed identity on printed p. 29 and Theorem 6.7 on printed p. 28. Its 28 November 2026 convention on printed p. 6 explains that displayed identities compare evaluated bimodule maps at the same boundary and that admissible indexed sums are evaluated pointwise. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf#page=29 https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf#page=6

The owner’s 27 November 2026 clarification, recorded in translation recheck request f13b4bd8ba9fe139, gives each marked crossing one finite complex linear label of termwise eligible group elements, including the zero label. The upper left and lower right projections require finite fibers for every label term, and their trace dots use the inverses of the stored multiplication parameters. Each canonical orbit drawing uses coefficient-one singleton labels.

The Lean proposition retains both typed drawings at the fixed ordered boundary. The simultaneous G × F action on input–output basis pairs uses left multiplication by G and inverse right multiplication by F. The supported-orbit sum retains a single PointwiseIndexedDrawing scope with one right drawing per supported orbit, using its projected pair stabilizer and matrix coefficient. The evaluations agree at every input. The finite-sum criterion uses a single IndexedDrawing scope and holds exactly when the orbit support is finite. The independently reviewed Lean proposition was retained verbatim and rechecked through the shared compilation slot.

The designated article defect report returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. No statement correction for this endpoint could be verified. https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem CaseFivePointwiseFiniteDiagramIdentity : ∀ {U : Type*} [Group U] (G A D F C E : Subgroup U)
    (a : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A G) (b : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding A D)
    (d : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding F D) (c : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding C G)
    (e : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding C E) (f : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding F E),
  let up := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.up U _
  let down := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.down U _
  let tensor := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor U _
  let comp := @MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp U _
  let ga := up a
  let ad := down b
  let df := up d
  let gc := up c
  let ce := down e
  let ef := up f
  let bottom := tensor ga (tensor ad df)
  let top := tensor gc (tensor ce ef)
  let X := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis bottom
  let Y := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis top
  let Pair := X.carrier × Y.carrier
  let input := fun (g : G) (x : D) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction a)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ad df)) g (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair b d x)
  let output := fun (g : G) (y : E) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction c)
      (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ce ef)) g (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair e f y)
  letI : MulAction (G × F) Pair :=
    { smul := fun q z => (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.act X q z.1, MackeyDiagrams.Biset.act Y q z.2)
      one_smul := fun z => Prod.ext (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.one_act X z.1)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.one_act Y z.2)
      mul_smul := fun q q' z => Prod.ext (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.mul_act X q q' z.1)
        (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.mul_act Y q q' z.2) }
  let orbit : Pair → Set Pair := MulAction.orbit (G × F)
  let stabilizer : Pair → Subgroup (G × F) := MulAction.stabilizer (G × F)
  let projected := fun z : Pair =>
    Subgroup.map (MonoidHom.comp (Subgroup.subtype F) (MonoidHom.snd G F)) (stabilizer z)
  let coefficient := fun (M : MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom Complex X Y) (z : Pair) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap M (Finsupp.single z.1 (1 : Complex)) z.2
  let MiddleLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp c k)
  let UpperLabel := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp e k) (comp f j)
  let ProjectionTerm := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed b d i j
  let drawId := fun {K H : Subgroup U} (p : MackeyDiagrams.Word K H) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id (R := Complex) p)
  let rightDrawing := fun (P : Subgroup U)
      (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
      (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (lower : List (Complex × ProjectionTerm P i j))
      (middle : List (Complex × MiddleLabel P i k))
      (upper : List (Complex × UpperLabel P j k)) =>
    let ai := up i
    let fj := down j
    let ck := up k
    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId ga)
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection b d i j lower))
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ga ai fj))
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp a i c k middle) (drawId fj))
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate gc ck fj))
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId gc)
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication e f k j upper))))) :
      MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
  let eval := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
    MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret drawing)
  let IsRightTerm := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
    ∃ (P : Subgroup U) (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A)
      (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F) (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
      (lower : List (Complex × ProjectionTerm P i j))
      (middle : List (Complex × MiddleLabel P i k))
      (upper : List (Complex × UpperLabel P j k)),
      drawing = rightDrawing P i j k lower middle upper
  ∀ (B : Subgroup U)
      (u : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding G B) (v : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding D B)
      (w : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding E B),
    let LeftUpper := MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed u w c e
    let leftDrawing := fun
        (rs : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp u a) (comp v b)))
        (ts : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp v d) (comp w f)))
        (ss : List (Complex × LeftUpper)) =>
      let ug := down u
      let dv := up v
      let ew := up w
      (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ga ad df))
        (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication u v a b rs) (drawId df))
          (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate ug dv df))
            (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal (drawId ug)
                (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp v d w f ts))
              (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
                (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ug ew ef))
                (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical
                  (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal
                    (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection u w c e ss) (drawId ef))
                  (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary
                    (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate gc ce ef))))))) :
        MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
    ∀ (rs : MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex (comp u a) (comp v b))
      (ts : MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex (comp v d) (comp w f))
      (ss : Finsupp LeftUpper Complex),
    let upperTerms := List.map (fun s => (ss s, s)) (Finset.toList (Finsupp.support ss))
    let M := eval (leftDrawing (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.terms rs)
      (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.terms ts) upperTerms)
    let supported := {O : Set Pair | ∃ z : Pair, O = orbit z ∧ coefficient M z ≠ 0}
    (∃ (diagram : supported → MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
        (weight : supported → Complex),
      (∀ O : supported,
        ∃ (r : D) (t : G) (s : E),
          let z := (input 1 r, output t s)
          let P := projected z
          O.val = orbit z ∧
          weight O = coefficient M z ∧
          ∃ (i : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P A) (j : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P F)
            (k : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding P C)
            (rDot : ProjectionTerm P i j) (tDot : MiddleLabel P i k) (sDot : UpperLabel P j k),
            (∀ h : P, (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom j h : U) = (h : U)) ∧
            MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element (MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.dot rDot) = r ∧
            MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element tDot = t ∧
            MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element sDot = s ∧
            diagram O = rightDrawing P i j k [(1, rDot)] [(1, tDot)] [(1, sDot)]) ∧
      let term := fun (O : supported) (x : Finsupp X.carrier Complex) =>
        weight O • MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (eval (diagram O)) x
      ∃ (finite : ∀ x : Finsupp X.carrier Complex, Set.Finite {O : supported | term O x ≠ 0}),
        let sum : MackeyDiagrams.PointwiseIndexedDrawing Complex bottom top supported :=
          ⟨fun O => MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (weight O) (diagram O), finite⟩
        ∀ x : Finsupp X.carrier Complex,
          MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap M x = sum.evalAt x) ∧
    ((∃ terms : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top),
        (∀ term ∈ terms, IsRightTerm term.2) ∧
        let drawing : MackeyDiagrams.IndexedDrawing Complex bottom top (Fin terms.length) :=
          ⟨Finset.univ, fun i => MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.scale (terms.get i).1 (terms.get i).2⟩
        MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap M = drawing.eval) ↔
      Set.Finite supported)
```

## CaseFiveRequiresTwoTerms: A Case 5 diagram requiring two terms

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Take \(U=D=E=C_2=\{1,g\}\) and \(G=A=C=F=1\), with inclusion labels.
Let \(L(r,t,s)\) and \(R(r,t,s)\) denote the left and right drawings
above with these vertex labels and with \(B=C_2,\ B'=1\), respectively.
Equation~(6.3) gives
\(L(1,1,1)=\id_{\C[C_2]}\). Every right diagram factors through
the one-dimensional space immediately above the first crossing:
its basis is \(G\times_{B'} F\), where \(G=F=B'=1\). Equation~(6.4) gives
\[
 L(1,1,1)=R(1,1,1)+R(g,1,g).
\]
Each right diagram selects and reinserts one of the two basis elements.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 6.5 (ex:case-five-two-terms), p. 27. The rendered diagrams on p. 27 and equations (6.3) and (6.4) fix the crossing order, inclusion labels, and basis conventions. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf

The owner’s 27 November 2026 clarification (translation recheck request f13b4bd8ba9fe139) governs the syntax. Each of the three marked crossings takes one finite complex label of termwise eligible group elements. Each projection term has finite-fiber evidence from the finiteness of its source basis. The merge and split identify the space above the first right crossing with the linearization of the basis G ×_{B′} F in the evaluation factorization. The statement preserves the left identity, the obstruction for every single right drawing, the two-term identity, and the basis action of the singleton drawings. Lean elaborated the statement through the shared compilation slot. A separate erasure check confirmed the three crossing kinds and their positions for arbitrary labels on both sides.

## CaseFiveRequiresInfiniteExpansion: An infinite expansion in Case 5

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Take \(U=B=G=C=D=E\) infinite cyclic, written multiplicatively,
and \(A=F=1\). The left diagram with inclusions and unit labels sends
\([g,x]\mapsto gx\) after identifying the target with \(\C[U]\).
Its reverse cup has index \(1\). On the right \(B'=1\) is forced.
Each right diagram vanishes unless \(x\) is one of the finitely many
crossing elements of its first crossing. The same holds for a finite sum.
Using \(L,R\) for the drawings with this boundary, the pointwise
finite identity is
\[
 L(1,1,1)=\sum_{x\in U} R(x,x,1).
\]
The term indexed by \(x\) selects second coordinate \(x\) and sends
\([g,x]\) to \(gx\).

The owner’s 27 November 2026 clarification in input.request governs dot syntax and is recorded at 2026-11-27T04:57:54.839065+00:00 in the project’s owner-clarification.json. A separate request ID is unavailable. The article remains the statement source. Each marked crossing carries a single finite complex label with termwise eligibility, including the zero label. Mixed projections use crossing elements with termwise finite-fiber evidence and inverse trace dots. The finite-sum obstruction ranges over the complete PlanarAtBoundary fiber of the right shape with the original boundary groups and embedding labels. The infinite sum keeps its pointwise-finite meaning on every input vector. The displayed full index type is retained in one PointwiseIndexedDrawing. Its stored finite-support condition only restricts evaluation at an input. [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem CaseFiveRequiresInfiniteExpansion : let U := Multiplicative Int
let P : Subgroup U := ⊤
let T : Subgroup U := ⊥
let p := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.id P
let a : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T P :=
  { toHom := Subgroup.inclusion bot_le
    hasRepresentative := ⟨1, fun _ => by simp⟩ }
let i := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.id T
let comp := @MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp U _
let up := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.up U _
let down := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.down U _
let tensor := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor U _
let stack := @MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical U _ Complex _
let beside := @MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal U _ Complex _
let plain := @MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary U _ Complex _
let ga := up a
let ad := down a
let df := up a
let gc := up p
let ce := down p
let ef := up a
let ai := up i
let fj := down i
let ck := up a
let bottom := tensor ga (tensor ad df)
let top := tensor gc (tensor ce ef)
let indexOne : (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom p).range.index = 1 := by
  change (MonoidHom.id P).range.index = 1
  rw [MonoidHom.range_eq_top_of_surjective (MonoidHom.id P) (fun x => ⟨x, rfl⟩),
    Subgroup.index_top]
let leftDot := MackeyDiagrams.Dot.id (comp p p)
let leftFinite :
    ∀ z, Set.Finite {w | MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedMultiplicationBasis p p p p leftDot w = z} := by
  intro z
  have finite : (MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom p).range.FiniteIndex :=
    ⟨by rw [indexOne]; decide⟩
  refine Set.Finite.subset (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.multiplicationCap_finiteFiber
    p finite (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedProduct p p z)) ?_
  intro w hw
  have hcap : MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedProduct p p
      (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedMultiplicationBasis p p p p leftDot w) =
      MackeyDiagrams.Generator.multiplicationCapBasis p w := by
    refine Quotient.inductionOn w (fun xy => ?_)
    change MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedProduct p p
      (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair p p (xy.1 * 1 * xy.2)) = xy.1 * xy.2
    rw [MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedProduct_mixedPair, mul_one]
  exact hcap.symm.trans (congrArg (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedProduct p p) hw)
let drawId := fun {K H : Subgroup U} (w : MackeyDiagrams.Word K H) =>
  plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id w)
let leftMixed := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication (R := Complex)
  p p a a [(1, MackeyDiagrams.Dot.id (comp p a))]
let leftParallel := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp (R := Complex)
  p a p a [(1, MackeyDiagrams.Dot.id (comp p a))]
let leftProject := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection (R := Complex)
  p p p p [(1, ⟨leftDot, leftFinite⟩)]
let left : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top :=
  stack (plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ga ad df))
    (stack (beside leftMixed (drawId df))
      (stack (plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate ce gc df))
        (stack (beside (drawId ce) leftParallel)
          (stack (plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ce gc ef))
            (stack (beside leftProject (drawId ef))
              (plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate gc ce ef)))))))
let dot := fun (b c : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T P) (x : P) =>
  ({ element := x
     intertwines := fun h => by
       have hh : h = 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
       simp [hh] } : MackeyDiagrams.Dot b c)
let Lower := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex (comp a i) (comp a i)
let Middle := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex (comp a i) (comp p a)
let Upper := MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel Complex (comp p a) (comp a i)
let rightFinite : ∀ (d : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp a i)) z,
    Set.Finite {w | MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedMultiplicationBasis a a i i d w = z} := by
  let : Finite (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ai fj)).carrier := by
    change Finite (Quotient (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.balance
      (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction i) (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.restriction i)))
    infer_instance
  intro d z
  exact Set.toFinite _
let right := fun (lower : Lower) (middle : Middle) (upper : Upper) =>
  let projectionTerms : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed a a i i) :=
    List.map (fun (term : Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp a i)) =>
      (term.1, (⟨term.2, rightFinite term.2⟩ : MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed a a i i)))
      (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.terms lower)
  let first := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection a a i i projectionTerms
  let second := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp a i p a
    (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.terms middle)
  let third := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication p a a i
    (MackeyDiagrams.DotLabel.terms upper)
  (stack (beside (drawId ga) first)
    (stack (plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate ga ai fj))
      (stack (beside second (drawId fj))
        (stack (plain (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate gc ck fj))
          (beside (drawId gc) third)))) :
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
let rightShape := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.planarShape (right 0 0 0)
let bottomBoundary := MackeyDiagrams.Word.boundary bottom
let topBoundary := MackeyDiagrams.Word.boundary top
let RightDrawing := MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary
  Complex bottomBoundary topBoundary rightShape
let rightAt := fun (lower : Lower) (middle : Middle) (upper : Upper) =>
  ({ bottom := bottom
     top := top
     diagram := right lower middle upper
     bottom_eq := rfl
     top_eq := rfl
     shape_eq := by rfl } : RightDrawing)
let rightTerm := fun r : P =>
  right (Finsupp.single (dot (comp a i) (comp a i) r) 1)
    (Finsupp.single (dot (comp a i) (comp p a) r) 1)
    (Finsupp.single (dot (comp p a) (comp a i) 1) 1)
let X := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis bottom
let Y := MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis top
let inputPair := fun g x : P =>
  MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction a)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ad df)) g (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair a a x)
let outputPair := fun h y : P =>
  MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction p)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor ce ef)) h (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair p a y)
let input := fun g x : P => Finsupp.single (inputPair g x) (1 : Complex)
let output := fun z : P => Finsupp.single (outputPair z 1) (1 : Complex)
let eval := fun (d : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
  MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap
    (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret d))
let evalAt := fun (d : MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram Complex
    (MackeyDiagrams.Boundary.word bottomBoundary) (MackeyDiagrams.Boundary.word topBoundary)) =>
  MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval
    (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.vertical
      (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Word.reorderToBoundary bottom))
      (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.vertical d
        (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Word.reorderFromBoundary top)))))
let interpretRight := fun (d : RightDrawing) =>
  MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary.interpret (s := rightShape) d
let rightSum := fun (terms : List (Complex × RightDrawing)) =>
  MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.linearCombination
    (List.map (fun term => (term.1, interpretRight term.2)) terms)
(MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom p).range.index = 1 ∧
  (∀ (Q : Subgroup U), MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding Q T → Q = T) ∧
  (∃ identify : Y.carrier ≃ P, ∀ h y : P, identify (outputPair h y) = h * y) ∧
  (∀ g x : P, eval left (input g x) = output (g * x)) ∧
  (∀ (lower : Lower) (middle : Middle) (upper : Upper) (g x : P),
    x ∉ Finset.image MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element (Finsupp.support lower) →
      eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.PlanarAtBoundary.diagram
        (rightAt lower middle upper)) (input g x) = 0) ∧
  (∀ d : RightDrawing, ∃ support : Finset P, ∀ g x : P, x ∉ support →
    evalAt (interpretRight d) (input g x) = 0) ∧
  (∀ terms : List (Complex × RightDrawing),
    (∃ support : Finset P, ∀ g x : P, x ∉ support →
      evalAt (rightSum terms) (input g x) = 0) ∧
    evalAt (rightSum terms) ≠ eval left) ∧
  (∀ r g x : P, eval (rightTerm r) (input g x) =
    (if x = r then output (g * x) else 0)) ∧
  (∃ finite : ∀ v : Finsupp X.carrier Complex,
      Set.Finite {x : P | eval (rightTerm x) v ≠ 0},
    let drawing : MackeyDiagrams.PointwiseIndexedDrawing Complex bottom top P :=
      ⟨rightTerm, finite⟩
    ∀ v : Finsupp X.carrier Complex, eval left v = drawing.evalAt v)
```

## CaseSixProjectionNoLeftReplacement: A Case 6 projection with no left replacement

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Use the boundary in Example~6.5. The right diagram \(R(1,1,1)\)
fixes \(1\) and sends \(g\) to \(0\). On the left \(B=C_2\) is forced
since it receives \(D\) and \(E\) and lies in \(U=C_2\).
All embeddings of \(C_2\) are identities, so
(6.3) sends \(x\) to \(s^{-1}rxt\)
for each group-element triple. These maps and all their finite
linear combinations commute with translation by \(g\). The right
map sends \(g\) to zero, while translating
its value at \(1\) gives \(g\). Thus no finite sum of left diagrams
gives the right map. All cups in this example have index at most \(2\).

```lean
theorem CaseSixProjectionNoLeftReplacement : let U := Multiplicative (ZMod 2)
let T : Subgroup U := ⊥
let H : Subgroup U := ⊤
let pack := fun x : U => (⟨x, Subgroup.mem_top x⟩ : H)
let g := pack (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZMod 2))
let unitEmbedding := MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.id T
let inclusion : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T H :=
  ⟨Subgroup.inclusion (show T ≤ H from bot_le), ⟨1, fun _ => by simp⟩⟩
let a := unitEmbedding
let b := inclusion
let d := inclusion
let c := unitEmbedding
let e := inclusion
let f := inclusion
let i := unitEmbedding
let j := unitEmbedding
let k := unitEmbedding
let up := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.up U _
let down := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.down U _
let tensor := @MackeyDiagrams.Word.tensor U _
let comp := @MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.comp U _
let hom := @MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding.toHom U _
let bottom := tensor (up a) (tensor (down b) (up d))
let top := tensor (up c) (tensor (down e) (up f))
let ordinary := @MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.ordinary U _ Complex _
let stack := @MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.vertical U _ Complex _
let beside := @MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.horizontal U _ Complex _
let straight := fun {K J : Subgroup U} (p : MackeyDiagrams.Word K J) =>
  ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.id p)
let onLeft := fun {K J J' L M : Subgroup U}
    {p : MackeyDiagrams.Word K J} {q : MackeyDiagrams.Word J L}
    {p' : MackeyDiagrams.Word K J'} {q' : MackeyDiagrams.Word J' L}
    (w : MackeyDiagrams.Word L M)
    (crossing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex (tensor p q) (tensor p' q')) =>
  stack (ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.unassociate p q w))
    (stack (beside crossing (straight w)) (ordinary (MackeyDiagrams.Diagram.associate p' q' w)))
let left := fun {B : Subgroup U}
    (α : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T B) (β γ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H B)
    (r : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp α a) (comp β b)))
    (t : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp β d) (comp γ f)))
    (s : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed α γ c e)) =>
  (stack
    (onLeft (up d) (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication α β a b r))
    (stack (beside (straight (down α)) (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp β d γ f t))
      (onLeft (up f) (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection α γ c e s))) :
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
let IsLeft := fun (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top) =>
  ∃ (B : Subgroup U) (α : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T B)
    (β γ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H B)
    (r : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp α a) (comp β b)))
    (t : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp β d) (comp γ f)))
    (s : List (Complex × MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed α γ c e)),
    drawing = left α β γ r t s
let right := fun (r : MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed b d i j)
    (t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp c k))
    (s : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp e k) (comp f j)) =>
  (stack (beside (straight (up a)) (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.compactProjection b d i j [(1, r)]))
    (stack (onLeft (down j) (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.parallelUp a i c k [(1, t)]))
      (beside (straight (up c)) (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.mixedMultiplication e f k j [(1, s)]))) :
    MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top)
let input := fun x : H => Finsupp.single
  (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction a)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor (down b) (up d))) 1
    (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair b d x)) (1 : Complex)
let output := fun x : H => Finsupp.single
  (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.pair (MackeyDiagrams.Biset.induction c)
    (MackeyDiagrams.Word.basis (tensor (down e) (up f))) 1
    (MackeyDiagrams.Generator.mixedPair e f x)) (1 : Complex)
let evaluate := fun {p q : MackeyDiagrams.Word T T}
    (drawing : MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex p q) =>
  MackeyDiagrams.Biset.Hom.toLinearMap
    (MackeyDiagrams.ScopedDiagram.eval (MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing.interpret drawing))
let translate := fun (a₀ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T T)
    (b₀ d₀ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T H) =>
  let dot : MackeyDiagrams.Dot d₀ d₀ := ⟨g, fun x => mul_comm (hom d₀ x) g⟩

let translationOut := translate c e f
let Summand := Complex × MackeyDiagrams.LabelledDrawing Complex bottom top
let sumLeft := fun (terms : List Summand) =>

    MackeyDiagrams.IndexedDrawing Complex bottom top (Fin terms.length))
(0 < Subgroup.index (MonoidHom.range (hom e)) ∧ Subgroup.index (MonoidHom.range (hom e)) ≤ 2) ∧
(0 < Subgroup.index (MonoidHom.range (hom j)) ∧ Subgroup.index (MonoidHom.range (hom j)) ≤ 2) ∧
(∀ (B : Subgroup U) (α : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding T B)
    (β γ : MackeyDiagrams.ConjEmbedding H B),
  B = H ∧
  (∀ x : H, (hom β x : U) = (x : U) ∧ (hom γ x : U) = (x : U)) ∧
  (∀ (r : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp α a) (comp β b))
      (t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp β d) (comp γ f))
      (s : MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed α γ c e) (x : H),

      output ((pack (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element (MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.dot s) : U))⁻¹ *
        pack (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element r : U) * x * pack (MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t : U)))) ∧
∃ (r : MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.Mixed b d i j)
    (t : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp a i) (comp c k))
    (s : MackeyDiagrams.Dot (comp e k) (comp f j)),
  MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element (MackeyDiagrams.ProjectionDot.dot r) = 1 ∧
  MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element t = 1 ∧ MackeyDiagrams.Dot.element s = 1 ∧
  let R := evaluate (right r t s)
  R (input 1) = output 1 ∧ R (input g) = 0 ∧
  translationOut (R (input 1)) = output g ∧
  LinearMap.comp R translationIn ≠ LinearMap.comp translationOut R ∧
  (∀ (terms : List Summand), (∀ term ∈ terms, IsLeft term.2) →
    LinearMap.comp ((sumLeft terms).eval) translationIn =
      LinearMap.comp translationOut ((sumLeft terms).eval)) ∧
  (∀ (terms : List Summand), (∀ term ∈ terms, IsLeft term.2) → (sumLeft terms).eval ≠ R)
```

## ParabolicBlockOperationExample: Conjugation, intersection, and generation

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Take
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A&=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{4,5\}),\\
 B&=\operatorname{Sym}(\{2,3,4\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{6,7\}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Use singleton blocks for the remaining points in \(\{1,\ldots,7\}\).

\emph{Conjugation.} For \(\alpha=(1\,4\,6)\), the two nonsingleton
blocks of \(A\) map to \(\{2,3,4\}\) and \(\{5,6\}\), so
\[
 \cg{\alpha}{A}=
 \operatorname{Sym}(\{2,3,4\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{5,6\}).
\]

\emph{Intersection.} The only intersection of blocks with at least
two points is \(\{1,2,3\}\cap\{2,3,4\}=\{2,3\}\). Hence
\(A\cap B=\operatorname{Sym}(\{2,3\})\).

\emph{Subgroup generated by a union.} The block \(\{2,3,4\}\)
overlaps both nonsingleton blocks of \(A\), so their common union
is \(\{1,2,3,4,5\}\). The block \(\{6,7\}\) meets only its two
singleton blocks on the \(A\) side. Thus
\[
 \langle A\cup B\rangle
 =\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,3,4,5\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{6,7\}).
\]
For instance, the join contains \((1\,5)\), obtained by taking
endpoint transpositions along a path of overlapping blocks.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.1 [ex:parabolic-block-operations], p. 29](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.1 [ex:parabolic-block-operations], p. 29. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte, and the article webpage gives the same example. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404 with and without a trailing slash. The task context supplies no statement correction for this example. Both block families include the prescribed singleton blocks. Each factor fixes its complement in Nat pointwise, so all groups in the calculation consist of finitely supported permutations. The supremum of the disjoint block factors represents their product. The join of A and B is the subgroup generated by their union. The product of swaps defining α sends 1 to 4, 4 to 6, and 6 to 1. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ParabolicBlockOperationExample : let blockSym : Finset Nat → Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) :=
  fun S => MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ S))
let blocksA : Finset (Finset Nat) := {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5}, {6}, {7}}
let blocksB : Finset (Finset Nat) := {{2, 3, 4}, {6, 7}, {1}, {5}}
let A := iSup (fun S : ↥blocksA => blockSym (Subtype.val S))
let B := iSup (fun S : ↥blocksB => blockSym (Subtype.val S))
let α : Equiv.Perm Nat := Equiv.swap 1 4 * Equiv.swap 4 6
Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj α)) A =
    (blockSym {2, 3, 4} ⊔ blockSym {5, 6}) ∧
  A ⊓ B = blockSym {2, 3} ∧
  A ⊔ B = (blockSym {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} ⊔ blockSym {6, 7}) ∧
  Equiv.swap (1 : Nat) 5 ∈ A ⊔ B
```

## ParabolicDoubleCosetRepresentatives: Double coset representatives

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

First let \(G=\operatorname{Sym}(X)\). Write \(K=\prod_i\operatorname{Sym}(X_i)\)
and \(H=\prod_j\operatorname{Sym}(Y_j)\), with singleton blocks added so that
both partitions cover \(X\). Order each list of blocks and order the points
within each block by their natural order in \(\mathbb N\).

Make a tableau whose \(i\)-th row has positions labeled by the points of
\(X_i\). In the initial tableau \(t_0\), the box at position \(x\) has
entry \(j\) if \(x\in Y_j\). A permutation \(\sigma\in G\) sends the
entry at \(x\) to position \(\sigma(x)\). Write \(R_{ij}\) for the number
of entries \(j\) in row \(i\) of \(\sigma t_0\).

The classification is due to James and Kerber [4, Thm.~1.3.10].

The map
\[
 K\sigma H\longmapsto (R_{ij}),
 \qquad R_{ij}=|X_i\cap\sigma(Y_j)|
\]
is a bijection onto the nonnegative integer matrices with row sums
\(|X_i|\) and column sums \(|Y_j|\). For a given matrix, construct
a representative as follows.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Split the ordered block \(X_i\) into consecutive pieces of sizes
\(R_{i1},R_{i2},\ldots\). The \(j\)-th piece consists of the positions
that will carry entry \(j\).
\item Split the ordered block \(Y_j\) into consecutive pieces of sizes
\(R_{1j},R_{2j},\ldots\). Map its \(i\)-th piece in order to the
\(j\)-th piece of \(X_i\).
\end{enumerate}

The matched pieces partition \(X\) on each side, so the prescribed
maps give a permutation. It sends exactly \(R_{ij}\) points from
\(Y_j\) into \(X_i\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Proposition 7.3 [prop:parabolic-double-cosets], p. 30 (related source excerpts on pp. 29–30)](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and no correction for this endpoint was available. Fin indices encode the chosen block orders, the covering partitions include the singleton blocks, and ranks within blocks use the natural order on Nat. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ParabolicDoubleCosetRepresentatives : ∀ (X : Finset Nat) (r c : Nat) (A : Fin r → Finset ↥X) (B : Fin c → Finset ↥X),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ i, x ∈ A i) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ j, x ∈ B j) →
  let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
  let blockSym := fun S : Finset ↥X =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
  let K : Subgroup G := iSup (fun i => blockSym (A i))
  let H : Subgroup G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (B j))
  let Mat := {R : Fin r → Fin c → Nat //
    (∀ i, Finset.sum Finset.univ (R i) = Finset.card (A i)) ∧
    (∀ j, Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun i => R i j) = Finset.card (B j))}
  let rank := fun (S : Finset ↥X) (x : ↥S) =>
    ((Finset.orderIsoOfFin S rfl).symm x).val
  ∃ classify : DoubleCoset.Quotient (K : Set G) (H : Set G) ≃ Mat,
    (∀ (σ : G) i j, (classify (DoubleCoset.mk K H σ)).val i j =
      Finset.card (A i ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B j))) ∧
    ∀ R : Mat, ∃ σ : G,
      DoubleCoset.mk K H σ = classify.symm R ∧
      ∀ (i : Fin r) (j : Fin c) (x : ↥(A i)) (y : ↥(B j)),
        σ y.val = x.val ↔
          ∃ k : Fin (R.val i j),
            rank (A i) x =
              Finset.sum (Finset.Iio j) (fun j' => R.val i j') + k.val ∧
            rank (B j) y =
              Finset.sum (Finset.Iio i) (fun i' => R.val i' j) + k.val
```

## ParabolicMackeyIntersectionBlocks: Block formula for the Mackey intersection of a tableau representative

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

First let \(G=\operatorname{Sym}(X)\). Write \(K=\prod_i\operatorname{Sym}(X_i)\)
and \(H=\prod_j\operatorname{Sym}(Y_j)\), with singleton blocks added so that
both partitions cover \(X\). Order each list of blocks and order the points
within each block by their natural order in \(\mathbb N\).

For any representative \(\sigma\), the Mackey intersection is
\[
 K\cap\sigma H\sigma^{-1}
   =\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Sym}(X_i\cap\sigma(Y_j)).
\]
This is the block-intersection formula of
Proposition~7.1 applied to \(K\) and
\(\sigma H\sigma^{-1}\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.2, after Proposition 7.3, p. 30](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, § 7.2, after Proposition 7.3, p. 30. The published PDF matches the project copy. The supplied defect report returned HTTP 404, and no correction for this endpoint was available in the task context. The covering partitions include the singleton blocks. Fin indices encode the chosen block orders, and points inherit the natural order on Nat. Every permutation represents its own double coset. The subgroup suprema give the products of disjoint block factors, each extended by the identity on its complement in X. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ParabolicMackeyIntersectionBlocks : ∀ (X : Finset Nat) (r c : Nat) (A : Fin r → Finset ↥X) (B : Fin c → Finset ↥X),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ i, x ∈ A i) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ j, x ∈ B j) →
  let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
  let blockSym := fun S : Finset ↥X =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
  let K : Subgroup G := iSup (fun i => blockSym (A i))
  let H : Subgroup G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (B j))
  ∀ σ : G,
    K ⊓ Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj σ)) H =
      iSup (fun i => iSup (fun j =>
        blockSym (A i ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B j))))
```

## TableauDoubleCosetRepresentativeInS6: A double-coset representative from a tableau

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

In \(S_6\) use the two subgroups
\[
\begin{aligned}
K&=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,2,4,5\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{3,6\}),\\
H&=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,3,5\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{2,4,6\}).
\end{aligned}
\]
For the matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\),
the first row receives one \(1\) at position \(1\). The second row
receives two \(1\)'s at positions \(3,6\). The ordered matching
gives \(\sigma=(5\,6)\), and its Mackey group is
\(\operatorname{Sym}(\{2,4,5\})\times\operatorname{Sym}(\{3,6\})\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.2 [ex:tableau-s6], p. 30](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Example 7.2 (ex:tableau-s6), p. 30, using the ordered block matching convention in § 7.2. The published PDF matches the project copy. The supplied defect report returned HTTP 404, and no correction for this example was available. Fin indices 0 and 1 encode the first and second blocks in the displayed order. The underlying points retain the labels 1 through 6 and are ordered by their natural order. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem TableauDoubleCosetRepresentativeInS6 : let X : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 6
let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
let block := fun (S : Finset Nat) =>
  Finset.filter (fun x : ↥X => Subtype.val x ∈ S) Finset.univ
let A : Fin 2 → Finset ↥X := fun i =>
  if i = 0 then block {1, 2, 4, 5} else block {3, 6}
let B : Fin 2 → Finset ↥X := fun j =>
  if j = 0 then block {1, 3, 5} else block {2, 4, 6}
let blockSym := fun (S : Finset ↥X) =>
  MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
let K : Subgroup G := iSup (fun i => blockSym (A i))
let H : Subgroup G := iSup (fun j => blockSym (B j))
let R : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Nat := fun i j =>
  if i = 0 then (if j = 0 then 1 else 3) else (if j = 0 then 2 else 0)
let rank := fun (S : Finset ↥X) (x : ↥S) =>
  Fin.val (OrderIso.symm (Finset.orderIsoOfFin S rfl) x)
let five : ↥X := ⟨5, Iff.mpr Finset.mem_Icc ⟨of_decide_eq_true rfl, of_decide_eq_true rfl⟩⟩
let six : ↥X := ⟨6, Iff.mpr Finset.mem_Icc ⟨of_decide_eq_true rfl, of_decide_eq_true rfl⟩⟩
∃ σ : G,
  (∀ i j, Finset.card (A i ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B j)) = R i j) ∧
  A 0 ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B 0) = block {1} ∧
  A 1 ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B 0) = block {3, 6} ∧
  (∀ (i j : Fin 2) (x : ↥(A i)) (y : ↥(B j)),
    σ (Subtype.val y) = Subtype.val x ↔
      ∃ k : Fin (R i j),
        rank (A i) x = Finset.sum (Finset.Iio j) (fun j' => R i j') + Fin.val k ∧
        rank (B j) y = Finset.sum (Finset.Iio i) (fun i' => R i' j) + Fin.val k) ∧
  σ = Equiv.swap five six ∧
  K ⊓ Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj σ)) H =
    blockSym (block {2, 4, 5}) ⊔ blockSym (block {3, 6})
```

## TwoBlockDoubleCosetMatrices: Classification of two-block double-coset matrices

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

When \(K\) and \(H\) each have two blocks in \(\operatorname{Sym}(X)\),
write \(n=|X|\), \(c=|X_1|\), and \(d=|Y_1|\). The matrices are precisely
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}
 a&c-a\\ d-a&n-c-d+a
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad \max(0,c+d-n)\le a\le\min(c,d),\qquad a\in\mathbb Z.
\]
The entry \(a\) determines the other three entries, and the bounds
make all four entries nonnegative.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.3, unnumbered, p. 30](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

The two ordered partitions of X include singleton blocks when needed to cover X. By Proposition 7.3, the range over permutation representatives is the range of double-coset matrices. Their entries are cardinalities viewed as integers, and the upper-left entry determines the unique parameter. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (A i)) →
  (∀ j, Finset.Nonempty (B j)) →
  Pairwise (fun i i' => Disjoint (A i) (A i')) →
  Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (B j) (B j')) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ i, x ∈ A i) →
  (∀ x : ↥X, ∃ j, x ∈ B j) →
  let n : Int := Int.ofNat (Finset.card X)
  let c : Int := Int.ofNat (Finset.card (A 0))
  let d : Int := Int.ofNat (Finset.card (B 0))
  ∀ R : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Int,
    (∃ σ : Equiv.Perm ↥X, ∀ i j, R i j =
      Int.ofNat (Finset.card (A i ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (B j)))) ↔
```

## StandardTwoBlockRepresentatives: Transposition representatives and Mackey blocks for standard two-block subgroups

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For standard two-block subgroups of \(S_n\), take
\(K=S_{n_1}\times S_{n-n_1}\) and \(H=S_{n_2}\times S_{n-n_2}\),
where \(1\le n_1,n_2<n\) and each first block begins at \(1\).
An alternative
set of representatives, convenient for computing the intersections,
is
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 m=\min(n_1,n_2,n-\max(n_1,n_2)),\qquad \sigma_0=1,\\
 \sigma_i=(\min(n_1,n_2)-i+1,\ \max(n_1,n_2)+i)\,\sigma_{i-1}
     \qquad (1\le i\le m).
 \end{gathered}
\]
The transpositions are disjoint. Each one takes a further point
of \(Y_1\) out of \(X_1\) and puts a point of its complement in
\(X_1\). Thus \(a_i=\min(n_1,n_2)-i\) takes every allowed value
exactly once. The four Mackey block sizes, in row order, are
\[
 a_i,\qquad n_1-a_i,\qquad n_2-a_i,\qquad n-n_1-n_2+a_i.
\]
The four intersections are intervals in the standard order, with
empty intervals omitted.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.3, unnumbered, pp. 30–31](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.3, unnumbered standard two-block representatives, pp. 30–31. The published PDF matches the project PDF byte for byte. The supplied defect report returned HTTP 404, and the available sources supply no correction for this endpoint. The ambient labels are 1 through n. The swap indexed by j in Fin m is the article’s swap at step j + 1. The four sizes are in row order, and the Mackey subgroup supremum ranges over the nonempty intersections. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem StandardTwoBlockRepresentatives : ∀ (n n1 n2 : Nat), 1 ≤ n1 → n1 < n → 1 ≤ n2 → n2 < n →
  let X : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 n
  let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
  let interval := fun lo hi : Nat =>
    Finset.filter (fun x : ↥X => lo ≤ x.val ∧ x.val ≤ hi) Finset.univ
  let XBlock : Fin 2 → Finset ↥X := fun r =>
    if r = 0 then interval 1 n1 else interval (n1 + 1) n
  let YBlock : Fin 2 → Finset ↥X := fun c =>
    if c = 0 then interval 1 n2 else interval (n2 + 1) n
  let blockSym := fun S : Finset ↥X =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
  let K : Subgroup G := iSup (fun r => blockSym (XBlock r))
  let H : Subgroup G := iSup (fun c => blockSym (YBlock c))
  let s := Nat.min n1 n2
  let t := Nat.max n1 n2
  let m := Nat.min s (n - t)
  let a : Fin (m + 1) → Int := fun i => Int.ofNat s - Int.ofNat i.val
  ∃ (left right : Fin m → ↥X) (σ : Fin (m + 1) → G),
    (∀ j : Fin m, (left j).val = s - j.val ∧ (right j).val = t + j.val + 1) ∧
    let τ : Fin m → G := fun j => Equiv.swap (left j) (right j)
    σ 0 = 1 ∧
    (∀ j : Fin m, σ (Fin.succ j) = τ j * σ (Fin.castSucc j)) ∧
    Pairwise (fun j k => Disjoint (Equiv.Perm.support (τ j)) (Equiv.Perm.support (τ k))) ∧
    Function.Bijective (fun i => DoubleCoset.mk K H (σ i)) ∧
    Set.BijOn a Set.univ
      (Set.Icc (max 0 (Int.ofNat n1 + Int.ofNat n2 - Int.ofNat n)) (Int.ofNat s)) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin (m + 1),
      let C : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Finset ↥X := fun r c =>
        XBlock r ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding (σ i)) (YBlock c)
      let size := fun r c => Int.ofNat (Finset.card (C r c))
      size 0 0 = a i ∧
      size 0 1 = Int.ofNat n1 - a i ∧
      size 1 0 = Int.ofNat n2 - a i ∧
      size 1 1 = Int.ofNat n - Int.ofNat n1 - Int.ofNat n2 + a i ∧
      (∀ r c, ∃ lo hi : Nat, C r c = interval lo hi) ∧
      K ⊓ Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj (σ i))) H =
        iSup (fun p : {p : Fin 2 × Fin 2 // Finset.Nonempty (C p.1 p.2)} =>
          blockSym (C p.val.1 p.val.2))
```

## EqualTwoBlockSubgroups: Equal two-block subgroups

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

For
\(K=H=S_n\times S_m\le S_{n+m}\), \(n\ge m\), the representatives
swap the last \(i\) points of the first block with the first
\(i\) points of the second block in reverse order. The intersection
group is \(S_{n-i}\times S_i\times S_i\times S_{m-i}\),
with a zero-size factor interpreted as the trivial group.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.4 [ex:equal-two-blocks], p. 31](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.4 [ex:equal-two-blocks], p. 31. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and the available sources give no correction for this endpoint. The preceding paragraph of § 7.3 supplies the two nonempty, one-based standard blocks. The swap indexed by j pairs label n − j with label n + j + 1, giving the specified reverse pairing. The four supported subgroups are in the article’s row order, and Equiv.Perm (Fin 0) is the trivial factor. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem EqualTwoBlockSubgroups : ∀ (n m : Nat), 1 ≤ m → m ≤ n →
  let X : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 (n + m)
  let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
  let interval := fun lo hi : Nat =>
    Finset.filter (fun x : ↥X => lo ≤ Subtype.val x ∧ Subtype.val x ≤ hi) Finset.univ
  let block : Fin 2 → Finset ↥X := fun r =>
    if r = 0 then interval 1 n else interval (n + 1) (n + m)
  let blockSym := fun S : Finset ↥X =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
  let K : Subgroup G := iSup (fun r => blockSym (block r))
  ∃ (left right : Fin m → ↥X) (σ : Fin (m + 1) → G),
    (∀ j : Fin m,
      Subtype.val (left j) = n - Fin.val j ∧
      Subtype.val (right j) = n + Fin.val j + 1) ∧
    σ 0 = 1 ∧
    (∀ j : Fin m, σ (Fin.succ j) =
      Equiv.swap (left j) (right j) * σ (Fin.castSucc j)) ∧
    Function.Bijective (fun i => DoubleCoset.mk K K (σ i)) ∧
    ∀ i : Fin (m + 1),
      let k := Fin.val i
      let L : Subgroup G := K ⊓ Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj (σ i))) K
      L = ((blockSym (interval 1 (n - k)) ⊔
            blockSym (interval (n - k + 1) n)) ⊔
            blockSym (interval (n + 1) (n + k))) ⊔
            blockSym (interval (n + k + 1) (n + m)) ∧
      Nonempty (MulEquiv ↥L
        (Equiv.Perm (Fin (n - k)) × Equiv.Perm (Fin k) ×
          Equiv.Perm (Fin k) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (m - k))))
```

## MackeyConjugationExchangesFactors: Conjugation exchanging two factors

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Even when \(\sigma_i^{-1}L_i\sigma_i=L_i\), the conjugation can
exchange factors. For \(n=m=2\), the representative with \(i=2\)
exchanges the two \(S_2\) factors.

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.5 [ex:two-block-factor-exchange], p. 31](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, Example 7.5 [ex:two-block-factor-exchange], p. 31. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The supplied defect report returned HTTP 404. The accessible article and HTML edition agree, and no correction was available for this example. The statement uses the one-based blocks {1, 2} and {3, 4} and the reverse pairing from Example 7.4. It identifies the Mackey intersection with the two-block subgroup and states that inverse conjugation preserves the intersection and exchanges its two supported factors. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem MackeyConjugationExchangesFactors : let X : Finset Nat := Finset.Icc 1 4
let G := Equiv.Perm ↥X
let interval := fun lo hi : Nat =>
  Finset.filter (fun x : ↥X => lo ≤ Subtype.val x ∧ Subtype.val x ≤ hi) Finset.univ
let blockSym := fun S : Finset ↥X =>
  MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun x : ↥X => x ∈ S))
let A : Subgroup G := blockSym (interval 1 2)
let B : Subgroup G := blockSym (interval 3 4)
let K : Subgroup G := A ⊔ B
let point := fun j : Nat => fun h : 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ 4 =>
  (⟨j, Finset.mem_Icc.mpr h⟩ : ↥X)
let σ : G :=
  Equiv.swap (point 1 (by decide)) (point 4 (by decide)) *
    Equiv.swap (point 2 (by decide)) (point 3 (by decide))
let L : Subgroup G := K ⊓ Subgroup.map (MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj σ)) K
let conjugate := MulEquiv.toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj (σ⁻¹))
L = K ∧
  Subgroup.map conjugate L = L ∧
  Subgroup.map conjugate A = B ∧
  Subgroup.map conjugate B = A
```

## ProductParabolicDoubleCosets: Product formula for parabolic double cosets and representatives

Main result; compiled and axiom-checked.

### Article

Now let \(G=\prod_i G_i\) be a finite parabolic group.
On the finite set partitioned by the blocks of \(G\), each block
of \(K\) or \(H\) lies inside a block of \(G\), since every
transposition within it belongs to \(G\). Thus
\(K=\prod_i K_i\), \(H=\prod_i H_i\), where \(K_i,H_i\le G_i\)
are the restrictions to that block. Double coset equality is
componentwise, giving
\[
 K\backslash G/H \cong \prod_i K_i\backslash G_i/H_i .
\]
Choose one matrix and its representative in each \(G_i\) and
multiply those representatives, whose supports are disjoint.
This gives every double coset once. A factor with \(K_i=G_i\)
or \(H_i=G_i\) contributes only the representative \(1\).

[Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.3, unnumbered, p. 31](https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf)

### Alphabeta Math

No Alphabeta Math source recorded.

### Lean statement

Translation source: article. Ian Xiao, Bimodule String Diagrams and the Generalized Mackey Decomposition, § 7.3, unnumbered product formula, p. 31, with the ordered tableau convention of Proposition 7.3. The published PDF matches the project copy byte for byte. The supplied defect-report URL returned HTTP 404, and no correction for this endpoint was available. The common finite set includes singleton padding, and local block orders inherit the chosen orders on the two block lists. The representative choice uses the ordered tableau matching in each factor where both subgroups are proper and the article’s identity normalization where either subgroup is the whole factor. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf [Defect report](https://getcurious.cc/articles/math-bimodule-string-diagrams/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects).

```lean
theorem ProductParabolicDoubleCosets : ∀ (X : Finset Nat) (g r c : Nat)
    (D : Fin g → Finset Nat) (A : Fin r → Finset Nat) (B : Fin c → Finset Nat),
  (∀ i, Finset.Nonempty (D i)) →
  (∀ a, Finset.Nonempty (A a)) →
  (∀ b, Finset.Nonempty (B b)) →
  Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (D i) (D j)) →
  Pairwise (fun a a' => Disjoint (A a) (A a')) →
  Pairwise (fun b b' => Disjoint (B b) (B b')) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ i, n ∈ D i) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ a, n ∈ A a) →
  (∀ n : Nat, n ∈ X ↔ ∃ b, n ∈ B b) →
  let blockSym := fun S : Finset Nat =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ S))
  let G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) := iSup (fun i => blockSym (D i))
  let K₀ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) := iSup (fun a => blockSym (A a))
  let H₀ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Nat) := iSup (fun b => blockSym (B b))
  K₀ ≤ G → H₀ ≤ G →
  let K := Subgroup.comap (Subgroup.subtype G) K₀
  let H := Subgroup.comap (Subgroup.subtype G) H₀
  let Gᵢ := fun i : Fin g => Equiv.Perm ↥(D i)
  let rows := fun i : Fin g =>
    Finset.filter (fun a : Fin r => A a ⊆ D i) Finset.univ
  let cols := fun i : Fin g =>
    Finset.filter (fun b : Fin c => B b ⊆ D i) Finset.univ
  let row := fun (i : Fin g) (a : Fin (Finset.card (rows i))) =>
    Finset.subtype (fun n : Nat => n ∈ D i)
      (A ((Finset.orderIsoOfFin (rows i) rfl a).val))
  let col := fun (i : Fin g) (b : Fin (Finset.card (cols i))) =>
    Finset.subtype (fun n : Nat => n ∈ D i)
      (B ((Finset.orderIsoOfFin (cols i) rfl b).val))
  let localSym := fun (i : Fin g) (S : Finset ↥(D i)) =>
    MonoidHom.range (Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : ↥(D i) => n ∈ S))
  let Kᵢ := fun i : Fin g => iSup (fun a => localSym i (row i a))
  let Hᵢ := fun i : Fin g => iSup (fun b => localSym i (col i b))
  let Mat := fun i : Fin g =>
    {R : Fin (Finset.card (rows i)) → Fin (Finset.card (cols i)) → Nat //
      (∀ a, Finset.sum Finset.univ (R a) = Finset.card (row i a)) ∧
      (∀ b, Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun a => R a b) = Finset.card (col i b))}
  let rank := fun (i : Fin g) (S : Finset ↥(D i)) (x : ↥S) =>
    ((Finset.orderIsoOfFin S rfl).symm x).val
  let Q := DoubleCoset.Quotient (K : Set G) (H : Set G)
  let Qᵢ := fun i : Fin g => DoubleCoset.Quotient (Kᵢ i : Set (Gᵢ i)) (Hᵢ i : Set (Gᵢ i))
  let extend := fun (i : Fin g) (σ : Gᵢ i) =>
    Equiv.Perm.ofSubtype (p := fun n : Nat => n ∈ D i) σ
  (∀ a, ∃ i, A a ⊆ D i) ∧
  (∀ b, ∃ i, B b ⊆ D i) ∧
  ∃ (split : G ≃* (∀ i, Gᵢ i)) (quotientSplit : Q ≃ (∀ i, Qᵢ i))
    (classify : ∀ i, Qᵢ i ≃ Mat i) (localRep : ∀ i, Mat i → Gᵢ i)
    (rep : (∀ i, Mat i) → G),
    (∀ (σ : G) (i : Fin g) (x : ↥(D i)),
      (split σ i x).val = (σ : Equiv.Perm Nat) x.val) ∧
    (∀ σ : G, (σ ∈ K ↔ ∀ i, split σ i ∈ Kᵢ i) ∧
      (σ ∈ H ↔ ∀ i, split σ i ∈ Hᵢ i)) ∧
    (∀ (σ : G) i,
      quotientSplit (DoubleCoset.mk K H σ) i = DoubleCoset.mk (Kᵢ i) (Hᵢ i) (split σ i)) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin g) (σ : Gᵢ i) a b,
      (classify i (DoubleCoset.mk (Kᵢ i) (Hᵢ i) σ)).val a b =
        Finset.card (row i a ∩ Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding σ) (col i b))) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin g) (R : Mat i),
      DoubleCoset.mk (Kᵢ i) (Hᵢ i) (localRep i R) = (classify i).symm R) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin g) (R : Mat i), Kᵢ i ≠ ⊤ → Hᵢ i ≠ ⊤ →
      ∀ a b (x : ↥(row i a)) (y : ↥(col i b)),
        localRep i R y.val = x.val ↔
          ∃ k : Fin (R.val a b),
            rank i (row i a) x = Finset.sum (Finset.Iio b) (fun b' => R.val a b') + k.val ∧
            rank i (col i b) y = Finset.sum (Finset.Iio a) (fun a' => R.val a' b) + k.val) ∧
    (∀ i, (Kᵢ i = ⊤ ∨ Hᵢ i = ⊤) → ∀ R : Mat i, localRep i R = 1) ∧
    (∀ R : ∀ i, Mat i,
      Pairwise (fun i j =>
        Disjoint {n : Nat | extend i (localRep i (R i)) n ≠ n}
          {n : Nat | extend j (localRep j (R j)) n ≠ n})) ∧
    (∀ R : ∀ i, Mat i,
      (rep R : Equiv.Perm Nat) = List.prod (List.ofFn (fun i => extend i (localRep i (R i))))) ∧
    Function.Bijective (fun R => DoubleCoset.mk K H (rep R))
```
